item.title: [WSLS] Yamamoto is dominant again as Dodgers ride homers from Hernández and Freeman to 3-1 win over Braves
item.dc:creator: Charles Odum; Associated Press
item.description: ATLANTA – Yoshinobu Yamamoto felt trust from Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts when he remained in a crucial NL Division Series game after a stressful fifth inning. “I’d like to continue living up to the highest expectation,” Yamamoto said through a translator. Recommended Videos The right-hander from Japan continues to do more than just meet expectations in the postseason. Yamamoto struck out 10 in seven brilliant innings, Kiké Hernández hit a two-run homer and the Dodgers beat the Atlan
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA – Yoshinobu Yamamoto felt trust from Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts when he remained in a crucial NL Division Series game after a stressful fifth inning.
“I’d like to continue living up to the highest expectation,” Yamamoto said through a translator.
Recommended Videos
The right-hander from Japan continues to do more than just meet expectations in the postseason.
Yamamoto struck out 10 in seven brilliant innings, Kiké Hernández hit a two-run homer and the Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 3-1 on Tuesday night to take a 2-1 lead in their NL Division Series.
Yamamoto dominated his much-anticipated matchup with Atlanta ace Chris Sale, who allowed three runs and seven hits in five innings. Last year's World Series MVP permitted only four hits and one walk while improving to 8-1 with a 2.14 ERA in 11 career postseason outings, including 10 starts.
His 10 strikeouts were a postseason high for him.
“I was confident and able to control all my pitches today,” Yamamoto said.
The Dodgers can clinch the best-of-five series and take another step toward becoming the first National League team to win three consecutive World Series by beating the Braves again Wednesday night in Game 4.
Atlanta hoped giving Sale extra rest would be a winning formula in the pivotal third game. Instead, after stranding six runners in the first three innings, he gave up the two-run homer to Hernández and a solo shot to former Braves star Freddie Freeman in the fourth.
“He was still touching 100 (mph),” manager Walt Weiss said of Sale. “The stuff was fine. Like I said, maybe the command not perfect. It wasn’t bad. But they did a nice job against him.”
That was all the offensive support Yamamoto and relievers Tanner Scott and Edwin Díaz would need.
Ozzie Albies opened the Atlanta ninth with a double off the right-center wall against Díaz and moved to third on Michael Harris II's groundout. Díaz stranded the runner and earned a save when Mauricio Dubón fouled out to right field and Mike Yastrzemski grounded out to shortstop Mookie Betts.
A homer for the boo birds
Freeman said he didn't mind being booed by Atlanta fans in the sellout crowd of 42,420.
“I’ve got a gray uniform on,” Freeman said. “I expect boos. It’s OK. ... It’s all love. I still love everybody here and I’m looking forward to tomorrow.”
Dubón made a leaping catch over the left-field wall to rob Freeman of a home run in the third. Freeman wouldn't be denied an inning later. Hernández's homer to left drove in Andy Pages, who singled. One out later, Freeman pulled his 18th career postseason homer to right field for a 3-0 lead.
Lineup change
Roberts moved designated hitter Shohei Ohtani down to No. 5 in the lineup because Ohtani was 3 for 15 in his career against Sale. Ohtani went 0 for 4 with two strikeouts against Sale when the Dodgers lost 1-0 on Aug. 26 in Atlanta.
Roberts correctly predicted Ohtani would have opportunities with runners on base hitting lower in the order.
With runners on first and second in the first, Sale struck out Ohtani to end the inning. With two runners on base in the third, Ohtani reached on catcher's interference by Drake Baldwin to load the bases before Miguel Rojas ended the inning with a flyball to right field. Ohtani walked to lead off the eighth against Brent Suter, Atlanta's fourth pitcher.
Baldwin's bases-loaded grounder to first base drove in Dubón, who singled, in the fifth for Atlanta's only run.
Injury report
Rojas left during an at-bat in the eighth. The second baseman appeared to injure his back on a swing and was replaced by Tommy Edman. The Dodgers announced the injury as lower back pain.
Roberts said Rojas probably won't start on Wednesday and his availability off the bench will be determined before the game.
“I give him credit for conceding that at-bat,” Roberts said.
Weiss made a late change, moving Ronald Acuña Jr. from right field to designated hitter. Weiss said Acuña jammed his knee on a slide in Game 2. Acuña remained in the game but the knee was sore on Tuesday, leading to the lineup change.
Milestone win for Roberts
Roberts now has 71 career postseason wins, tying Tony La Russa for second-most in major league history. Joe Torre is first with 84.
Up next
Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle is expected to face Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow in Game 4 on Wednesday night. Mahle said Tuesday an abdominal pull is now a “non-issue.” He felt the pull before allowing one run in seven innings of a 4-3 loss to Philadelphia in 10 innings during the NL Wild Card Series last week.
___

item.title: [MLB.com] Dubón le niega un jonrón a Freeman... pero Freddie cobra revancha después
item.dc:creator: Paul Casella
item.description: Después de que Sale consiguiera cada uno de sus primeros seis outs por la vía del ponche en el Juego 3 de la SDLN contra los Dodgers, Dubón registró el primer out defensivo y lo hizo de manera espectacular. Con un corredor en primera y nadie fuera en la parte alta del tercer inning, la exsuperestrella de los Bravos Freddie Freeman conectó un batazo profundo hacia el jardín izquierdo que salió de su bate a 101.3 mph. Dubón siguió la trayectoria de la pelota hasta la pared y calculó perfectamente
item.content:encoded:
Después de que Sale consiguiera cada uno de sus primeros seis outs por la vía del ponche en el Juego 3 de la SDLN contra los Dodgers, Dubón registró el primer out defensivo y lo hizo de manera espectacular.
Con un corredor en primera y nadie fuera en la parte alta del tercer inning, la exsuperestrella de los Bravos Freddie Freeman conectó un batazo profundo hacia el jardín izquierdo que salió de su bate a 101.3 mph. Dubón siguió la trayectoria de la pelota hasta la pared y calculó perfectamente su salto para realizar la atrapada justo frente a un grupo de relevistas de los Dodgers, quienes se preparaban para que la bola cayera en el bullpen de los visitantes.
La atrapada de Dubón probablemente le robó un posible jonrón de dos carreras a Freeman, pero como mínimo evitó un extrabase y, casi con toda seguridad, una carrera o dos en el episodio.
Los Dodgers llenaron las bases gracias a un sencillo de Will Smith con dos outs y a que Shohei Ohtani llegó a salvo por interferencia del receptor, pero Sale salió ileso al hacer que Miguel Rojas conectara una línea al jardín derecho para terminar la entrada.
Antes de siquiera necesitar la ayuda de su defensa, Sale se unió a Mike Hampton (Juego 2 de la SDLN del 2003) como los únicos lanzadores de los Bravos en conseguir cada uno de sus primeros seis outs por la vía del ponche en un juego de postemporada.
Freeman se desquitó en su siguiente turno al bate, cuando disparó con autoridad un cuadrangular hacia el jardín derecho-central, el 18vo vuelacercas de su carrera en postemporada, para darle a los Dodgers una ventaja de 3-0.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers beat Braves on Kiké Hernández and Freddie Freeman homers, take 2-1 NLDS lead

item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
ATLANTA — The Dodgers went into Game 3 of the National League Division Series knowing they couldn’t be so reliant on the home run, especially with Braves ace Chris Sale on the mound. And yet, in a 3-1 win, it was the home run ball, paired with a masterful performance on the mound from right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto, that secured the victory.
The Dodgers pulled ahead to a 2-1 lead in the best-of-five series.
The Dodgers tried to score in other ways, putting on six baserunners in the first three innings of the game. But it didn’t work.
They failed to take advantage of some luck and poor defense from the Braves in the first inning, as Mookie Betts beat out a soft ground ball up the first base line and Teoscar Hernández reached on a fielding error by Braves shortstop Ha-Seong Kim.
Yoshinobu gives up four hits and strikes out 10 and Kiké Hernández hits a two-run home run to power the Dodgers to victory in Game 3 of the NLDS.
The lineup shuffling manager Dave Roberts did against Sale had superstar Shohei Ohtani, batting fifth, walking up to the plate with two outs and runners on first and second. His over-anxious approach at the plate so far this postseason followed him into the at-bat. And he struck out whiffing on a slider in the opposite batter’s box.
The next inning, Kyle Tucker hit a two-out single into left, baited Sale into picking over to first base twice, and then stole second. But he was stranded there, as Kiké Hernández went down swinging. All six of the Dodgers’ outs in the first two innings came via the strikeout.
In the third, the Dodgers loaded the bases. Mookie Betts started the effort with a double through the left side of the infield. And it looked for a moment as if Freddie Freeman had capitalized on the opportunity with a runner in scoring position.
He stayed back on a fastball and crushed it to deep left field, on a trajectory to just clear the short fence. But Braves left fielder Mauricio Dubón made a leaping catch, holding into the ball as he slammed into the wall.
Undeterred, the Dodgers kept putting runners on base. With two outs, Will Smith stayed through a slider to single. Ohtani clipped Braves catcher Drake Baldwin’s mitt and was awarded first base for catcher’s interference. Then Miguel Rojas, who’d exit the game in the eighth inning mid-at-bat with what the Dodgers called low back pain, hit a line drive that found leather to end the inning.
So, back to the long ball.
Perennial postseason hero Kiké Hernández delivered the first blow. With Andy Pages on first, after his first hit of the series, Hernández launched a changeup into the left-field stands. Then, two batters later, Freeman turned on an inside sinker and sent it over the right-field fence — where Dubón had no chance to track it down.
Game 3 was billed as a matchup between aces: Sale, whom the Braves tabbed for Tuesday because of his workload in their wild-card series, and Yamamoto, whom the Dodgers partially held back for the first two games with the NLCS in mind.
Yamamoto held up his end of the bargain, limiting the Braves to four hits and one run in seven innings.
He retired 10 of the first 11 batters he faced. The only baserunner in that time, Michael Harris II, bunted for a single. Yamamoto crashed hard, slipping on the slick grass as he tried to pivot but still managing to make a throw to first from the ground.
Shohei Ohtani is batting fifth in the lineup against Braves ace Chris Sale in Game 3 of the NLDS. He hasn’t hit fifth or lower in a starting lineup since 2020 with the Angels.
He only wavered in the fifth, loading the bases with a pair of singles and a four-pitch walk. The Braves’ batting order turned over, and Yamamoto got Baldwin to ground out to first, but that allowed a run. Then he induced Ronald Acuña Jr. to ground out to second to escape the jam. Rojas ranged to his left to field the ball and made an on-target throw even as he slipped on the grass in shallow right field.
Yamamoto didn’t allow another baserunner.
Left-handed reliever Tanner Scott served as the Dodgers’ setup man, throwing a hitless eighth. And right-hander Edwin Díaz came in for his first save opportunity since Aug. 14 against the Brewers.
He gave up a double off the wall to Ozzie Albies to open the inning but retired the next three batters.

item.content:encoded:
During the eighth inning of Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, Dodgers middle infielder Miguel Rojas exited the game.
Rojas was seen in visible discomfort after fouling off a fastball from Braves reliever Brent Suter.
Rojas started limping back toward the batter’s box and was immediately evaluated by a member of the Dodgers’ training staff and manager Dave Roberts.
Shortly after the injury, the Dodgers announced that Rojas was removed from the game due to lower back pain.
Tommy Edman replaced Rojas at second base.
Rojas went 0-for-3 before departing Tuesday. He has one hit in the series — a double in Saturday’s 5-3 victory.
Rojas is expected to retire after the season is over.
Rojas was a World Series hero last year after hitting a game-tying home run in Game 7 against the Blue Jays, sending the game to extra innings.
The Dodgers went on to win the game in the 11th when Will Smith hit a go-ahead home run.
In Tuesday’s game, the Dodgers’ offense popped off in the fourth inning, when Kiké Hernández and Freddie Freeman homered to give LA a 3-0 lead.
The Braves scored in the fifth when Drake Baldwin grounded out to first after Dodgers starting pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto loaded the bases.
Yamamoto finished with a career-high 10 strikeouts. He tossed 98 pitches in seven innings, giving up four hits, one run and one walk.

item.content:encoded:
Miguel Rojas was the hero for the Los Angeles Dodgers during the 2025 postseason, but his 2026 postseason is off to a much worse start.
The Dodgers infielder Rojas had to exit Tuesday’s NLDS Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves in the middle of an at-bat. During the eighth inning at Truist Park in Atlanta, Ga., Rojas fouled off a 1-0 pitch from Braves reliever Brent Suter and immediately came up grimacing.
Rojas was unable to finish his plate appearance and went on to walk off the field with trainers. Here is the video of Rojas’ injury.
Miguel Rojas exits the game after he appears to have injured his back on a swing https://t.co/Rmc25l0OkW
— Talkin’ Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) October 7, 2026
Dodgers teammate Tommy Edman replaced Rojas in the game, finishing out his at-bat and also taking Rojas’ place in the field. The Dodgers soon officially announced that Rojas had left the contest due to “low back pain.”
Now 37 years old, Rojas is a two-time Dodgers champion who is very beloved by the team’s fanbase. Most notably, Rojas was directly responsible for the Dodgers’ 2025 championship by famously hitting a game-tying ninth-inning home run in Game 7 of the World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays.
But Rojas is now only on a one-year deal with the Dodgers and previously announced that he intends for the 2026 season to be his last. As such, it remains to be seen if that was Rojas’ last-ever at-bat in Major League Baseball.

item.title: [MLB.com] Dodgers' HR barrage continues with October Kiké's return, Freddie avenging robbery
item.dc:creator: Courtney Hollmon
item.description: ATLANTA -- After three scoreless innings of tight pitching at Truist Park, the Dodgers broke NLDS Game 3 open with a pair of fourth-inning home runs against Braves ace Chris Sale. The two-homer frame marks only the second time in Chris Sale’s postseason career that he has allowed multiple home runs in a single start. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA -- After three scoreless innings of tight pitching at Truist Park, the Dodgers broke NLDS Game 3 open with a pair of fourth-inning home runs against Braves ace Chris Sale.
The two-homer frame marks only the second time in Chris Sale’s postseason career that he has allowed multiple home runs in a single start. It happened previously on April 1, 2023, when Sale was with the Red Sox.
Kiké Hernández provided the initial spark, crushing a 406-foot two-run shot to left field to break the scoreless tie and put Los Angeles on the board. Just two batters later, Freddie Freeman delivered a dose of sweet-swinging revenge. After having a potential home run robbed by left fielder Mauricio Dubón in the third inning, Freeman made sure there was no doubt on his next trip to the plate, launching a solo shot deep into right-center field to extend the lead to 3-0.
The pair of big flies extended a historic postseason trend for Los Angeles: All 10 of the Dodgers' runs scored so far this postseason have come via the home run, marking the longest streak to start a postseason in MLB history.
Both home runs also provided individual milestones in the October record books.
For Hernández, the blast marked his first home run of the 2026 postseason and the 17th of his career, continuing his reputation as a clutch playoff hitter -- "October Kiké," if you will. He went 1-for-4 with two strikeouts.
“Experience helps a lot," Hernández said postgame on FOX. "Coming through in big moments helps a lot. Understanding that you can do it in the bigger moments. This is what I grew up dreaming about, playing October baseball. ... I’ve been lucky enough to play for two organizations that have put me there, and given me opportunities, and I’ve made the best of them.”
Freeman’s solo shot was his second of the 2026 postseason and the 18th of his playoff career, tying him with seven others for 10th on the all-time postseason home run list, including teammate Max Muncy, who got there in Game 2 of the NLDS. Freeman went 1-for-4 with a walk and a strikeout.
"It’s an extremely hard at-bat for a lefty," Freeman said of facing Sale on FOX. "I always say, against him, you’ve got to be prepared to die. Really, that’s the mindset. If you pull off of him, you have no chance. He’s throwing behind you and if he hits you in the ear, you’ve got to be ok with it. That’s my mentality, and thankfully I was able to get a good swing on some balls tonight.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have had plenty of postseason heroes during their World Series runs in 2024 and 2025.
Last year, the biggest may have been backup infielder Miguel Rojas, who hit a game-tying home run in Game 7 against the Toronto Blue Jays in the ninth inning.
As a result, Rojas has continued to get opportunities in 2026 and was inserted into the starting lineup for Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves in this year's NLDS. He also started Game 2 in place of Max Muncy at third base.
Oct 6, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; ]Los Angeles Dodgers second baseman Miguel Rojas (72) throws to first base for an out against the Atlanta Braves during the first inning in game three of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Rojas was put in to hit against Braves left-hander Chris Sale given his platoon advantage as a right-handed hitter. It did not work out through his first three at-bats as he went 0-for-3 with a strikeout.
Rojas remained in the game for a fourth at-bat in the eighth inning against Braves reliever Brent Suter, who is also a southpaw.
Unfortunately, he did not finish the at-bat. After fouling off the second pitch he immediately reached for his lower back with his left arm.
A trainer came out to visit Rojas and after a brief discussion he was removed from the game with Tommy Edman taking over mid at-bat. Edman popped up shortly after. The Dodgers released an update shortly after. "Miguel Rojas left tonight's game with low back pain," the team wrote on X.
Latest Update on Miguel Rojas
During the broadcast, Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reported that Rojas originally suffered the setback while fielding a ground ball back in the 5th inning.
If Rojas' injury is serious enough to keep him out for the remainder of the NLDS, the Dodgers would have to replace him on the roster.
That would also keep him out of the NLCS should Los Angeles advance, which would be a huge loss given the postseason experience he brings.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas has exited Game 3 of the National League Division Series in the top of the eighth inning with an injury.
Rojas appeared to tweak his lower back on a swing and is now out of the game. He initially tweaked his back on a defensive play earlier in the game.
He was replaced by Tommy Edman, who popped out on the first pitch he saw.
Rojas drew the start with the left-handed Chris Sale on the mound. It was his second consecutive start after he got the nod in Game 2 with the lefty Ray Kerr starting.
After going 1-for-1 against Kerr before being replaced by Max Muncy, Rojas was 0-for-3 on Tuesday.
What is Miguel Rojas' Injury?
The Dodgers announced Rojas exited the game with low back pain.
Is Miguel Rojas Retiring After This Season?
Rojas is in the midst of what's expected to be his final season in Major League Baseball. The 37-year-old entered the year saying this would be his last. However, he then left the door open for a potential return in 2027 if the Dodgers won the World Series this year.
Before Tuesday's game, Rojas spoke to reporters and still didn't have a firm answer.
"I'm not thinking about that at all. I'm not thinking about my future or anything," Rojas said. "In regards to my retirement or stepping away from the game, I will never think about stepping away from the game because of my performance or my way to play my game. I think there's other things in life that I'm contemplating about that decision. But if I have to tell you right now, I'm not 100% like [Clayton] Kershaw was last year or others in the past that knew for sure they want to go after this year.
"For me it's more, I would say it's a 40/60 right now that I want to stay in the game and I want to play. But it's not about me. It's about the organization. It's about doing what we're supposed to do to help the team win this year. And then after that we will have conversations."
Rojas, who hit the game-tying home run in Game 7 of the 2025 World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays, had a strong season in 2026, appearing in 105 games and hitting .267 with and OPS of .703. He's still an elite defender in the infield.
Off the field, he's a leader in the Dodgers clubhouse.
Manager Dave Roberts will have an update on his veteran after the game.

item.content:encoded:
Freddie Freeman and Kiké Hernández continue to add to their postseason résumés.
An inning after Freeman was denied an opposite-field home run over the left field wall at Truist Park by Mauricio Dubón, he thought he might try hitting one right.
But Hernandez needed to show off his bat first.
The two got the Dodgers on the board, to give them a 3-0 lead in the fourth inning of the NLDS, by hitting home runs over the walls in left and right field.
Hernández saw an 89 MPH changeup come his way by Braves starting pitcher Chris Sale and sent it 406 feet out of the park for a two-run homer. One batter later, Freeman obliterated a 96 MPH sinker and sent it screaming off the bat at 103 MPH for 399 feet.
Sale managed to get out of the inning in the following at-bat, but at first glance, it looked he was going to gve up another homer.
Teoscar Hernández just came short of Sale’s slider out of the park, after hard-hitting Sale at 108 MPH.
Both Freeman and Hernandez, continue to show why they are dominant in October, as both of them have had playoff heroics.
Freeman has a career batting average of .268 with 82 hits, 17 home runs, and 40 RBI through 81 postseason games.
Kiké Hernández has a career average of .272 with 80 hits and 16 home runs, with 42 RBIs in the postseason.
The combination of Hernández and Freeman came on the same day; manager Dave Roberts made a surprising decision to bump four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani down to the fifth hole in the Dodgers lineup and have Freeman hitting second, behind Mookie Betts, while Hernández was hitting ninth.
So far, his decision is paying off as Los Angeles holds a 3-1 lead against the Braves.

item.content:encoded:
In a game that could have a massive shift in momentum in either direction for both teams, the Atlanta Braves bring future HOFer Chris Sale to the mound amidst one of the best seasons of his career against Yoshinobu Yamamoto during the best season of his young career.
The last time these two pitchers faced off the Braves beat the Dodgers 1-0 when Chris Sale pitched a complete game shutout on August twenty-seventh. A repeat of that exact result is slim, but if Sale could pitch a long game today, it would be welcomed among the bullpen that has already had back-to-back games where they carried the load.
Drake Baldwin was the offensive hero the last time the Braves faced Yamamoto with a solo shot that was the only run of the game.
First pitch is at 6:00 pm EDT. Follow along in the comments.

item.content:encoded:
When will Dodgers' Tarik Skubal pitch next in NLDS? Here's the latest update appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are currently gearing up for Game 3 of their NLDS series against the Atlanta Braves on Tuesday afternoon on the road. The Dodgers are currently tied 1-1 with Atlanta after dropping a frustrating contest in Game 2 at home over the weekend.
The Dodgers won Game 1 of this series thanks in large part to a dominant pitching performance from ace Tarik Skubal, and now, the latest reporting has revealed when Skubal could be on the mound again for Los Angeles.
"Tarik Skubal throwing bullpen session in preparation for his next start…possibly Game 5," reported David Vassegh of AM 570 LA Sports on X, formerly Twitter.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Of course, if the Dodgers have their way, they'll win the next two games in Atlanta and avoid a Game 5 altogether, in which case Skubal would likely be the starter for Game 1 of the ensuing NLCS.
However, Los Angeles certainly has their work cut out for them in order to make that scenario a reality. Los Angeles' main hitters, headlined by Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani, have largely been dormant so far in this series, with the team mustering just two runs in Sunday's loss to Atlanta despite the Braves running out an all-bullpen lineup.
On Tuesday, Los Angeles will face off against the formidable Chris Sale, who is coming off a long rest after Walt Weiss opted not to rush him back in Game 2 in a gutsy move that ended up paying off.
The Dodgers will certainly want to see their bats come to life in Game 3 to retake control of the series.
Game 3 between the Dodgers and Braves is slated to get underway at 6:00 pm ET from Atlanta.
Related: Why Joe Davis isn't on broadcast for Fox's Dodgers-Braves NLDS Game 3

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Freddie Freeman not adding to narrative of facing Braves in postseason
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers and Atlanta Braves are facing off for the sixth time in MLB postseason history, but their latest meeting comes with an interesting twist. It’s the first time Freddie Freeman is playing his former team in October since signing with the Dodgers prior to the 2022 season. Freeman enjoyed a decorated 12-year career with the Braves, earning five All-Star Game selections, winning the 2020 NL MVP and leading them to a World Series title in 2021. It was widely expected that Freema
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and Atlanta Braves are facing off for the sixth time in MLB postseason history, but their latest meeting comes with an interesting twist.
It’s the first time Freddie Freeman is playing his former team in October since signing with the Dodgers prior to the 2022 season.
Freeman enjoyed a decorated 12-year career with the Braves, earning five All-Star Game selections, winning the 2020 NL MVP and leading them to a World Series title in 2021. It was widely expected that Freeman and the Braves would work out a new contract in free agency, but that never came to fruition due to a reported disagreement over the inclusion of a sixth year.
Freeman understands the significance of playing the Braves in the postseason but doesn’t want to make a big deal out of it, via Bob Nightengale of USA Today.
“I’m going to try and not treat it any differently, and nor should anybody else treat anything differently,’’ Freeman told USA TODAY Sports and MLB.com outside the Dodgers’ clubhouse. “I understand it will be a storyline. I get it, but it is five years later. But I’m not going to try and look at it any differently. It’s another team that I’m trying to get through to win another championship, and I know they’re thinking the same thing.
“It’s not the Los Angeles Freddies, you know? But I understand. I get the storyline. And it’s an easy storyline. So, I try not to think about it like that. Come game time, I don’t think anybody’s going to be worrying about it. We could talk about it now, but by (Saturday), I don’t think anybody’s going to be worrying about who played for what team.”
Freeman will always have a special place in his heart for the Braves, but he is rightfully choosing to treat the NLDS like any other playoff series as a way to not let his personal history become a distraction.
It took Freeman a while to completely move on from the Braves, but he has since become a huge part of the Dodgers’ identity and is responsible for some of the biggest moments in franchise playoff history.
Braves appreciate Freddie Freeman’s replacement
When it became clear that they wouldn’t resolve their contract dispute with Freeman, the Braves moved on by acquiring All-Star first baseman Matt Olson. The Atlanta native has done an exceptional job replacing Freeman and earned praise from manager Walt Weiss.
“Matt had a lot on his plate when he first got here. He was replacing an icon,” Weiss began. “I think we got the only guy that could do it, the only guy that could step in that role at that time, and Matt’s been a superstar for us.
“Freddie, obviously, he’s a Hall of Famer. I still stay in touch with Freddie quite often. It’s always good to see him, but tough facing him when he’s on the other side because he’s such a good player. Like I said, I think Matt’s the only guy that could have pulled this off to replace that guy. He’s done it very well.”

item.title: [Heavy.com] Los Angeles Dodgers Make Sudden Freddie Freeman Move Before Braves Game
item.dc:creator: Cole Sullivan
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are tied with the Atlanta Braves at one game apiece in their best-of-five series in the NLDS. On Tuesday night, the two teams will meet for Game 3 at Truist Park in Atlanta, with the Braves sending out left-handed ace Chris Sale while L.A. will start right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto in what should be one of the best pitching matchups we’ve seen so far this postseason. Ahead of the game, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made some major lineup changes, including one involving ve
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are tied with the Atlanta Braves at one game apiece in their best-of-five series in the NLDS.
On Tuesday night, the two teams will meet for Game 3 at Truist Park in Atlanta, with the Braves sending out left-handed ace Chris Sale while L.A. will start right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto in what should be one of the best pitching matchups we’ve seen so far this postseason.
Ahead of the game, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made some major lineup changes, including one involving veteran slugger Freddie Freeman.
Dodgers Announce Freeman Move
With Shohei Ohtani struggling at the plate recently, Roberts decided to move him down to the No. 5 spot in the lineup Tuesday night.
As a result, Freeman will move up from the cleanup spot to the No. 2 spot, while Mookie Betts remains in the leadoff spot.
Teoscar Hernandez and Will Smith will fill the No. 3 and No. 4 spots, while the back end of the order will remain fairly close to what the Dodgers have used recently, despite bringing Andy Pages back into the lineup.
Here’s the full Dodgers lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Dodgers 10/6 M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B T. Hernández LF W. Smith C S. Ohtani DH M. Rojas 2B A. Pages CF K. Tucker RF E. Hernández 3B Y. Yamamoto SP.”

Freeman’s 2026 Postseason
While it’s only been two games, Freeman has been one of the most consistent bats in the Dodgers’ lineup against his former team.
He’s recorded three hits across seven at-bats, including two on Sunday, one of which was a home run.
Freeman spent the first 12 years of his MLB career with the Braves and became one of the greatest players in franchise history. Now, he’ll play the next two games in a ballpark he called home for more than a decade.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Shohei Ohtani dropped to fifth in Dodgers' batting order for Game 3 of NLDS vs. Braves
item.dc:creator: Chris Cwik
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are pushing two-way star Shohei Ohtani to fifth in the batting order following a tepid start to the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves. After hitting second in the first two games of the series, Ohtani was dropped to fifth ahead of Game 3 on Tuesday. Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Teoscar Hernández and Will Smith will hit ahead of Ohtani in Game 3. In the two previous games in the series, Betts led off and Ohtani hit second. Per The Athletic's Fabi
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are pushing two-way star Shohei Ohtani to fifth in the batting order following a tepid start to the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves.
After hitting second in the first two games of the series, Ohtani was dropped to fifth ahead of Game 3 on Tuesday. Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Teoscar Hernández and Will Smith will hit ahead of Ohtani in Game 3.
In the two previous games in the series, Betts led off and Ohtani hit second.
Per The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya, Dodgers managers Dave Roberts told reporters that the move to fifth would be just for Tuesday's game against Braves ace Chris Sale. A lefty, Sale has been notoriously tough against left-handed batters over his career.
Roberts added that when he approached Ohtani about moving down in the order on Monday, Ohtani responded that he'd considered suggesting doing so in September as he struggled through injuries.
Hitting fifth is unusual for Ohtani, who hasn't hit that low since 2020, when he was a member of the Los Angeles Angels.
Ohtani hasn't been terrible in the first two games of the series, going 2-for-8 with two strikeouts. But other members of the team have outperformed the slugger in the NLDS. Freeman and Hernández, in particular, have ignited the Dodgers' offense. Smith, however, is hitless in eight at-bats thus far.
At the plate, Ohtani has been worse against lefties over his career, though he still has an excellent .853 OPS against them. That's actually higher than Smith's career OPS against left-handers.
Ohtani, however, came into the playoffs battling multiple injuries. On Friday, he acknowledged that left knee and right biceps issues will impact him throughout the postseason. Those same issues seemed to affect Ohtani in the second half, as he hit .241/.322/.472 in August before collapsing with a .200/.300/.233 line in eight games in September. At that point, the team put Ohtani on the injured list to give him time to recover for the playoffs.
Now that the playoffs are here, the Dodgers will try to ease Ohtani into a bigger role. While he hit second in the order early in the NLDS, a combination of his performance and Sale's presence on the mound will drop Ohtani much lower than he has hit in recent seasons.

item.title: [ABC7 Los Angeles] Dodgers' Kyle Tucker exits win vs. Twins with low back spasms
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS -- Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Kyle Tucker was removed from Monday's game against the Minnesota Twins in the second inning because of low back spasms. Tucker walked with one out in the second and ran lightly to second base on Tommy Edman's single to right field. Then, Tucker was replaced by pinch runner Alex Call. Tucker stayed in the dugout, standing up next to dugout fence before heading into the clubhouse after the inning was over. "I really felt it when I went out for defense
item.content:encoded:
MINNEAPOLIS -- Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Kyle Tucker was removed from Monday's game against the Minnesota Twins in the second inning because of low back spasms.
Tucker walked with one out in the second and ran lightly to second base on Tommy Edman's single to right field. Then, Tucker was replaced by pinch runner Alex Call. Tucker stayed in the dugout, standing up next to dugout fence before heading into the clubhouse after the inning was over.
"I really felt it when I went out for defense in between innings in the first," Tucker said. "Went out there and just tried to hope that it could kind of calm down, or go away or something and I could just keep playing through it. ... On the bases and stuff, it was kind of still sticking around, still kind of there."
Manager Dave Roberts said he considered Tucker day-to-day. The outfielder said, "just got to kind of see how it goes tomorrow," regarding his status.
After signing a four-year, $240 million contract with Los Angeles in January, Tucker has played in 75 of the Dodgers' 79 games this season. But he has hit just .234 with six home runs and 40 RBIs. The .234 average is his lowest since hitting .141 in 28 games as a rookie in Houston in 2018. He has hit at least 22 homers in each of the past five seasons.
The Dodgers also pulled catcher Dalton Rushing in the bottom of the third to rule out a concussion. Roberts said Rushing passed concussion testing, but the catcher has to retake the test 24 hours later and probably will be out of Tuesday's lineup. He was replaced by Chuckie Robinson and Roberts said the team probably would add another player in case Rushing is unavailable.
Los Angeles was already without No. 1 catcher Will Smith, who is on the 10-day IL because of neck inflammation.

item.title: [ABC7 Los Angeles] Dodgers land two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal in blockbuster deadline deal, sources say
item.dc:creator: Alden Gonzalez

Their farm system was too good, their goals were too lofty, their rotation had become too uncertain. On Saturday night, a day and a half before the trade deadline, they pulled it off. The Dodgers acquired Skubal, the reigning back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner, from
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- For as much as they might have downplayed the possibility behind closed doors, the Los Angeles Dodgers were long seen by rival executives as overwhelming favorites to land generational ace Tarik Skubal. Their farm system was too good, their goals were too lofty, their rotation had become too uncertain.
On Saturday night, a day and a half before the trade deadline, they pulled it off.
The Dodgers acquired Skubal, the reigning back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner, from the Detroit Tigers for a package of three prospects: outfielder Zhyir Hope, and right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.
Skubal, a 29-year-old pending free agent, will now headline what was arguably already the best rotation in the sport. Alongside him will be Yoshinobu Yamamoto, making a strong case for a Cy Young of his own, followed by Blake Snell, Shohei Ohtani and Tyler Glasnow, all of whom are in varying stages of returning from injury.
The Dodgers had long touted their depth as a reason they didn't necessarily need Skubal. Snell, who has made one start all year, is expected to rejoin the rotation after his next rehab outing. Glasnow, out since May 6 with back spasms, will begin a minor league rehab assignment next week. And though Ohtani is still troubled by a sore left knee that only seems to bother him on the mound, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said earlier this week he fully expects him to pitch in October.
The Game 1 starter, though, will be Skubal, who might be the best pitcher in the world.
Skubal boasts a 2.79 ERA in 16 starts this year, striking out 116 batters and issuing 14 walks in 96 innings. The only thing that could stop him were bone chips that began to cause irritation in his left elbow in late April. Skubal underwent a less-invasive, revolutionary NanoScope procedure and returned in about six weeks. His ERA in July is 2.03. And as he addressed the media in the visiting clubhouse at Sutter Health Park in Sacramento late Saturday night, moments after being informed of the trade, Skubal at one point got choked up.
"Going into the season, this isn't what I planned on doing," Skubal said before getting on the verge of tears while reflecting on his time in Detroit. "But circumstances change, situations change. I'm very appreciative of everything that the Tigers have done for me."
A late bloomer who lasted until the ninth round of the 2018 draft, Skubal began to emerge as one of the game's most talented pitchers in 2022 and 2023 and took it to another level thereafter. From 2024 to 2025, Skubal went 31-10 with a 2.30 ERA and a whopping 469 strikeouts in 387 innings. His 12.6 FanGraphs wins above replacement led all major league pitchers.
When Skubal and members of the Tigers' front office exchanged arbitration figures in the ensuing offseason, the two sides were $13 million apart. An independent arbitrator ruled in favor of Skubal and his agent, Scott Boras, rewarding him a $32 million salary as he headed into his free-agent year.
Rumors had swirled throughout the offseason that the Tigers would trade him then. Instead, they doubled down, signing fellow starter Framber Valdez to a three-year, $115 million contract with the hope of winning the AL Central. Instead, the Tigers flopped. By the end of May, they were tied with the Colorado Rockies for the worst record in the majors, prompting executives throughout the industry to assume Skubal would be traded.
The Tigers proceeded to win 28 of their next 46 games, and suddenly it seemed as if Skubal might stay. But their momentum ran out. The Tigers lost back-to-back games to the last-place Kansas City Royals over the weekend and dropped two of three to the Baltimore Orioles thereafter. The last of those losses, on Wednesday night, saw Skubal take the mound and record his 1,000th career strikeout, then sit in the dugout while his team blew a 7-0 lead.
After it was over, the Tigers were seven games below .500, six games out of first place and three games out of a wild-card spot.
To many observing Skubal's availability, it was a death knell to his time in Detroit.
The Atlanta Braves, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers, New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays were all in on Skubal to some extent, with the Brewers, deep in prospects, the favorites among that group. But the Dodgers were the clear frontrunners all along. And now they'll add Skubal to a laundry list of talent they've acquired from the outside over the years, following Ohtani, Snell, Yamamoto, Glasnow, Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and, this offseason, Edwin Diaz and Kyle Tucker.
The vast majority of those players came via free agency. The Dodgers loathe the high asking prices at midseason. But in getting Skubal, they parted from an outfield group that is stocked with talent -- one that is still headlined by Josue DePaula, a consensus top-25 prospect, along with Eduardo Quintero, ranked 45th on Kiley McDaniel's latest ESPN rankings. They also maintain all of their young major league starting pitching, namely Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan and Roki Sasaki.
In Hope and Ryan, though, the Tigers came away with two top-50 prospects.
Hope, 21, was slashing .293/.369/.530 with 23 home runs and 18 stolen bases for the Dodgers' Double-A affiliate and brings explosive power from the left side, top-tier speed and an ability to handle center field.
Ryan, 27, made a brief stint in the major leagues in 2024, putting up a 1.33 ERA in four starts. He then underwent a prolonged rehab from Tommy John surgery and has made eight starts in Triple-A, putting up a 4.46 ERA. He has been out since the middle of June with a hamstring injury, but McDaniel ranked him 49th in his midseason top 50 in May.
Smith, 21, was a third-round pick out of high school in 2023 who has put up a 3.88 ERA in 19 starts at the Class A level this season.
In three months, Skubal will head into the open market with the chance of signing the most lucrative deal ever rewarded to a starting pitcher. Before then, he will join a Dodgers club that boasts the highest run-differential and second-best record in the major leagues -- and help them try to become the first team in NL history to win three consecutive championships.
Asked his thoughts about joining the Dodgers, Skubal took about 15 seconds to compose himself before saying: "Yeah, it's exciting. I'm excited. They've got a good group."

item.title: [roundtable.io] Freeman Wants Dodgers to Find Ways to Score Without Home Runs
item.dc:creator: Anthony Arroyo
item.description: Freddie Freeman believes the Los Angeles Dodgers need to find more ways to manufacture offense after falling to the Atlanta Braves 3-2. Both teams have received strong pitching through the opening two games of the series, making consistent offense difficult to produce. Freeman believes the Dodgers need to create more opportunities, get runners on base and deliver the timely hit when those chances arise. The Dodgers have already demonstrated an ability to produce runs through the home run, but Fr
item.content:encoded:
Freddie Freeman believes the Los Angeles Dodgers need to find more ways to manufacture offense after falling to the Atlanta Braves 3-2.
Both teams have received strong pitching through the opening two games of the series, making consistent offense difficult to produce. Freeman believes the Dodgers need to create more opportunities, get runners on base and deliver the timely hit when those chances arise.
The Dodgers have already demonstrated an ability to produce runs through the home run, but Freeman sees manufacturing offense as an important part of their approach moving forward.
Atlanta's bullpen creates challenges
Atlanta used multiple pitchers throughout Game 2, creating a difficult matchup for the Dodgers' lineup.
Freeman acknowledged how challenging it can be to face a different arm repeatedly throughout a game. Each pitcher can bring a different combination of velocity, movement and release point, forcing hitters to adjust from one at-bat to the next.
That approach helped the Braves escape several important situations and keep the Dodgers from building a larger offensive threat. Ultimately, the Dodgers would finish 0-for-8 with runners in scoring position, leaving seven runners on base.
Atlanta's pitching staff has been able to limit Los Angeles through the first two games, contributing to two closely contested games. Freeman expects that challenge to continue as the series moves forward.
Dodgers need to capitalize on opportunities
While the Dodgers struggled to produce consistently, Freeman noted that the team did have opportunities during Game 2.
The difficulty comes from stringing together enough hits to turn those opportunities into multiple runs. In the postseason, where the quality of pitching is often at its highest, putting together several consecutive hits can be especially difficult.
That makes timely hitting even more important.
The Dodgers do not necessarily need to radically change their offensive approach. Instead, Freeman believes the lineup needs to continue controlling the strike zone and trusting its individual plans at the plate.
Freeman feeling good at the plate
Freeman also enters the next stage of the series feeling positive about his swing.
After a productive stretch leading into the postseason, the veteran first baseman believes he has been seeing the ball well through the opening games. He hopes to carry that consistency into the upcoming road portion of the series.
For Freeman, the key is maintaining the same approach rather than becoming overly aggressive in an attempt to create more offense.
The Dodgers' hitters will have to balance that patience with the need to capitalize when opportunities arise.
With the series now tied 1-1, Los Angeles heads into its next game needing to find additional ways to score. Freeman believes the answer is not abandoning the team's approach, but executing it better when the biggest opportunities arrive.

item.content:encoded:
As Shohei Ohtani works his way back to being in top form on the baseball diamond, the star continues to make off-field moves. Through the first two games of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves, Ohtani is hitting .250 with two hits and two strikeouts.
During the Dodgers’ run in the MLB playoffs, New Balance announced that Ohtani’s signature clothing line is now available in select markets.
“Shop the latest styles from the Shohei Ohtani Signature Collection,” New Balance noted in an October 3, Instagram post featuring Ohtani.
“Available now in select markets.”
Additionally, Chandler Bats announced that select fans can purchase a game-model bat designed for Ohtani. These will be a hot commodity as only 1,000 are being released.
“The bat behind the player who changed the game,” Chandler Bats noted in an October 1, Instagram post tagging Ohtani.
“Introducing the SO17.4 Limited Edition — built to @shoheiohtani game-model specifications and crafted by Chandler, available to the world for the first time,” Chandler Bats added.
“Only 1,000 will be made. Sign up to be the first to know at the link in bio.”
Shohei Ohtani’s Contract With Dodgers Includes $68 Million Deferred Annually Starting in 2034
Ohtani signed a massive 10-year, $700 million contract with the Dodgers that is slated to go through the 2033 season. One of the interesting aspects of Ohtani’s deal is that a large portion of the money is deferred.
According to Spotrac, Ohtani will receive $68 million annually from 2034 through 2043. It will be interesting to see what impact this will have on the Dodgers’ potential roster moves during this future time period.
With the way Ohtani’s deal is structured, it allowed the Dodgers to be more aggressive at the MLB trade deadline landing star pitcher Tarik Skubal as one example.
Dodgers Star Shohei Ohtani Is Projected to be MLB’s Top Earner in 2026 at $127 Million
SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – SEPTEMBER 25: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers walks back to the dugout after striking out against the San Francisco Giants in the top of the eighth inning at Oracle Park on September 25, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images)
Ohtani is projected to earn $127 million in 2026, the highest of any baseball player, per Forbes. The star is projected to earn $125 million through endorsements and business ventures compared to $2 million with the Dodgers.
“It’s no wonder that brands are still clamoring for his services, and he recently added a partnership hawking Japanese firm Kirin’s immune health supplements to his long list of sponsors,” Forbes detailed.
“With support like that, Ohtani’s $127 million estimated earnings will exceed the combined totals of the Nos. 2 and 3 players on this year’s Forbes list, with Cody Bellinger and Kyle Tucker set to bank $112.5 million between them.
Injuries have complicated the star’s 2026 campaign, but Ohtani is a rare phenom with the ability to be both an elite hitter and pitcher. This is only going to continue to allow Ohtani’s net worth to grow.

item.content:encoded:
By BETH HARRIS
PASADENA, Calif. (AP) — Fred Claire, who parlayed early jobs as a sports writer and editor into a 30-year career with the Los Angeles Dodgers in public relations and as a World Series-winning general manager, has died. He was 91.
Claire died Monday, on his 91st birthday, in Pasadena, the team announced Tuesday. Claire had entered hospice care recently.
In January 2015, at age 80, Claire was diagnosed with squamous cell skin cancer on his lip. He had the cells removed, but the cancer later returned in his jaw and again in his neck. He had surgery to remove a nerve on the left side of his face along with several lymph nodes. He underwent radiation, chemotherapy and immunotherapy as part of his 11-year journey with cancer.
He would jog regularly during his years on the road as the Dodgers general manager and said he was diligent about wearing sun screen except on his lips.
“Fred brought many victories and Dodger legends to our franchise, as well as the 1988 World Series title,” team president and CEO Stan Kasten said in a statement, “and we are forever grateful for his leadership during such a memorable era.”
From sports writing to public relations
Claire was covering the Dodgers during spring training in Florida for the Long Beach Press-Telegram in 1969 when one of the team’s public relations assistants was fired.
He expressed interest in the job and was hired that July. He was promoted to vice president of public relations and promotions in 1975.
During his tenure, Claire was instrumental in creating the Dodger Blue branding and Think Blue campaign. The club drew 3.3 million fans in 1978, the first MLB team to exceed 3 million. He also hired announcer Ross Porter, who worked for the team from 1977 until being let go in 2004.
In 1976, Chicago Cubs outfielder Rick Monday ran over and saved an American flag from being burned on the Dodger Stadium field by two spectators. Claire directed the message board operator to type the words: “Rick Monday……You Made a Great Play” on the board.
Becoming Dodgers GM after a scandal
In April 1987, a public relations firestorm occurred over comments 70-year-old general manager Al Campanis made on ABC’s “Nightline.”
Campanis, who was white, was asked by host Ted Koppel about the lack of Black people in significant positions of authority in baseball.
“I truly believe they may not have some of the necessities to be, let’s say, a field manager, or perhaps, a general manager,” Campanis said. “Why are Black people not good swimmers? Because they don’t have buoyancy.”
Campanis had agreed to the interview without telling anyone in the Dodgers organization. Claire awoke the next day to a story about Campanis’ comments in the newspaper.
“I couldn’t believe what I was reading,” he wrote in his 2004 memoir.
Campanis had been Jackie Robinson’s roommate when the two were in the minor leagues in 1946, and he tutored Robinson in transitioning from shortstop to second base. Robinson broke baseball’s color barrier with the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1947.
“Those who knew Al expressed shock. There had never been a hint of bigotry in anything he had ever said or done,” Claire wrote. “In my view, what Al had attempted to do that night was to defend his beloved game of baseball in an area where there was no defense.”
Campanis was fired after two decades as GM. Team owner Peter O’Malley handed control of one of the most storied teams in baseball to Claire. He accepted on the condition that he would have total and complete responsibility for baseball operations.
Claire wasn’t intimidated, either, having been involved in discussions regarding free agents, arbitration and team payroll since becoming a team vice president in 1975.
In Claire’s first full season as GM, the Dodgers finished with a 73-89 record in 1987. O’Malley informed Claire he was considering bringing in a more experienced person for the job. He called the New York Mets and asked for permission to speak to Joe McIlvaine, but was denied. O’Malley decided to stick with Claire.
“Fred was a talented team player and everyone in the organization enjoyed working with him,” O’Malley said in a statement.
Winning 1988 World Series
In January 1988, Claire signed Kirk Gibson and the outfielder made a huge difference in the Dodgers winning the World Series in five games over the heavily favored Oakland Athletics that fall. An injured Gibson hobbled to the plate as a pinch-hitter in the bottom of the ninth inning with the Dodgers trailing 4-3 in Game 1. He launched a two-strike, two-run homer — one of the most dramatic moments in baseball history — off closer Dennis Eckersley into the right field seats to win the game, 5-4.
Claire was named baseball’s executive of the year, an award previously won by such Dodger greats as Larry MacPhail, Branch Rickey, Walter O’Malley and Buzzie Bavasi.
The Dodgers returned to the playoffs just twice over the next decade, losing in the first round both times. It would be another 32 years before the Dodgers won the World Series again.
Good trades and bad ones, too
Among the trades that Claire was most proud of during his tenure as GM were those that brought John Shelby, Tim Belcher, Alfredo Griffin, Jay Howell, Jesse Orosco and John Tudor to Los Angeles — all of which had a connection with the 1988 World Series championship. He also traded for future Hall of Famer Eddie Murray in 1988 and again in 1997.
Two trades that Claire regretted were sending pitcher Pedro Martinez to the Montreal Expos and acquiring Eric Davis from Cincinnati. Martinez went on to win three Cy Young Awards with the Boston Red Sox, while Davis played two injury-plagued seasons in Los Angeles.
Dodgers sold, Piazza traded behind Claire’s back
The O’Malley family sold the team to Rupert Murdoch’s Fox Entertainment Group in March 1998.
Two months later, future Hall of Fame catcher and fan favorite Mike Piazza was traded to the Florida Marlins in a stunning seven-player deal struck without Claire’s knowledge. It was pulled off by Fox television executive Chase Carey, who Claire said, was pursuing a regional TV sports channel in Florida and wanted the Marlins to be part of it.
“The seven-player trade was, first and foremost, a television deal. The new team owner simply did not understand the structure of a baseball team and the importance of a franchise player,” Claire wrote. “My reaction to the trade cost me my position with the Dodgers.”
Claire, along with manager Bill Russell, was fired by Fox on June 21, 1998, the same day Campanis died. Former Dodgers manager Tommy Lasorda took over as interim GM.
Claire never took another full-time job in baseball but stayed connected with the sport through a column and radio show for MLB.com, as a consultant for sports-related companies and by co-founding a baseball analytics company. He taught sports business courses at Caltech, the University of Southern California and Long Beach State.
Love of baseball began as a kid in Ohio
Born Fredic Marston Claire on Oct. 5, 1935, in Jamestown, Ohio, he cultivated his love of baseball while attending Cincinnati Reds games with his family at Crosley Field. He moved to Torrance, California, at age 15. He graduated from Torrance High, where he played junior varsity baseball and basketball. He graduated from San Jose State University with a journalism degree.
His first job out of college was as a sports writer for the Whittier Daily News at $65 a week. During his time with the Progress-Bulletin in Pomona, he wrote the game story on the Dodgers winning Game 3 of the 1959 World Series against the Chicago White Sox, the team’s first World Series win after moving to Los Angeles.
He later covered the then-California Angels for the Long Beach Press-Telegram and became the paper’s beat writer for the Dodgers in 1969.
He is survived by wife Sheryl and children Jeff, Jennifer and Kim.
___

item.title: [Heavy.com] Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Andy Pages News Before Pivotal Braves Game
item.dc:creator: TJ French
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 26: Will Smith #16 of the Los Angeles Dodgers celebrates with Andy Pages #44 after scoring in the top of the fourth inning against the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park on September 26, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) If the Los Angeles Dodgers want to advance in the MLB playoffs, their hitters are going to have to get going. Currently, the NLDS between the Braves and Dodgers is knotted 1-1, but the series is s
item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 26: Will Smith #16 of the Los Angeles Dodgers celebrates with Andy Pages #44 after scoring in the top of the fourth inning against the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park on September 26, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images)
If the Los Angeles Dodgers want to advance in the MLB playoffs, their hitters are going to have to get going.
Currently, the NLDS between the Braves and Dodgers is knotted 1-1, but the series is shifting to Atlanta, which may give the Braves a slight advantage.
Before the pivotal Game Three between the Dodgers and Braves, LA’s manager, Dave Roberts, announced a piece of Andy Pages lineup news.
Andy Pages Will be in Dodgers Lineup Against Chris Sale
If you are not aware, the Atlanta Braves are throwing ace starter Chris Sale in Game Three, which means a tall task is ahead for Dodgers hitters.
Andy Pages, who has notably been struggling in the MLB playoffs over the last two years, will be in the lineup against Sale on Tuesday, per Dave Roberts.
@DodgersNation wrote: “Andy Pages will be in the Dodgers NLDS Game 3 lineup today despite his 0-for-7 start to the postseason, per Dave Roberts.”
Roberts also noted (about Pages):
“I’m going to continue to give Andy a leash. I believe in him.”
Andy Pages had a stellar regular season for the Dodgers, but a wrist injury left him sidelined for most of September, and now he’s started to struggle at the plate.
“Andy Pages in his postseason career: Began 1-for-10 (.282 OPS). *2024 NLCS Game 5: 3 hits, 2 HR. Since then: 4-for-63 (.185 OPS). Among 590 players with 80+ PA in the postseason, his .343 OPS ranks 589th”
GettyLOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – AUGUST 15: Andy Pages #44 of the Los Angeles Dodgers warms up before the starts of an inning against the Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
Andy Pages played in 134 games for the Dodgers in the regular season. He posted a bWAR of 6.0, which is a very strong mark.
He batted .274 with 26 doubles, 23 home runs, and an OPS+ of 122 while playing a very strong defensive center field.
Pages was named to the All-Star team for the first in his career back in July, but all the regular-season awards/accolades go out the window during the MLB playoffs.
TJ French covers the MLB for Heavy. TJ is a graduate of the University of Georgia. He has 2+ years of writing experience.
Follow TJ French on X: @tj_french5 More about TJ French
