Projecting the Dodgers' NLDS roster with Josue De Paula
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers get to kick back and watch as eight teams duke it out to move on to their respective League Division Series this week. The Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies will go head-to-head in the NL Wild Card Series before one of them moves on to try and topple LA.
One would think that this Dodgers team would have everything buttoned up well ahead of the NLDS, but there are still a couple of key questions to be answered.
Projecting the Dodgers' NLDS roster with Josue De Paula called upon
Catchers (2): Will Smith, Hunter Feduccia
For some reason, the Dodgers decided to carry three catchers on their Wild Card and NLDS rosters last year — Smith, Dalton Rushing, and Ben Rortvedt — but adjusted ahead of the NLCS by shedding Rushing, who received just one at-bat in the NLDS but otherwise rode the bench.
Rortvedt didn't get a start or even substitution after Game 2 of the NLDS with Smith slowly coming back from injury at the beginning of the postseason. Feduccia figures to play a similar break-glass-in-case-of-emergency role. As a lefty, he could get a start and then an early pull depending on matchups but, barring disaster, it's mostly going to be Smith's show.
Designated hitters (2): Shohei Ohtani, Josue De Paula
The Dodgers clearly want to find a way to bring De Paula with them in October, even if only as a lingering threat on their bench. They're reportedly not entertaining putting him in the outfield at all, and it's not hard to see why. Even if they're confident they'll be able to fix his defense in time, they can't afford any leakage in the postseason.
Ohtani is still shaking off the cobwebs from his 15-day IL stint. He picked up a few hits with promising exit velocity in his return against the San Diego Padres and later against the San Francisco Giants, but there are still question marks around what version of him we might see this postseason.
Infielders (6): Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Tommy Edman, Max Muncy, Miguel Rojas, Kiké Hernández
A notable exclusion here is Hyeseong Kim. Although he's in the running to get a spot on the bench and exclusively come into games to pinch-run or for reassurances on defense, there's still a chance he doesn't make the roster if the Dodgers are set on carrying 13 pitchers. Edman and Hernández, though lacking the same speed as Kim, can still offer the same defensive versatility.
Outfielders (3): Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Teoscar Hernández
Pages might've found himself in the same boat as Ohtani, but he announced his return to the Dodgers after a month-long IL stint in a big way, hitting .333 with a 1.180 OPS, two homers, and five RBI against the Padres and Giants. No doubt Dave Roberts and Andrew Friedman breathed a massive sigh of relief.
Alex Call will be the odd man out. He was on all four of LA's playoff rosters last year and received sporadic appearances throughout the month, but that was when Michael Conforto was still on the payroll. Tucker and Hernández have certainly had their ups-and-downs this season, but the Dodgers would never seriously consider leaving them out.
Starters (4): Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal, Tyler Glasnow
There's not much to say about what's probably the best rotation going into the postseason. Snell and Glasnow have both battled injury this season but came back when the Dodgers needed them most. It might be too much to ask that any of Yamamoto, Snell, or Glasnow replicate their dominance from last year, but they'll certainly try.
Relievers: (9): Tanner Scott, Roki Sasaki, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Justin Wrobleski, Edwin Díaz, Kris Bubic, Edgardo Henriquez
Just like 2025, this is where things get dicey. The Dodgers' bullpen isn't quite as banged up or as unreliable as they were last year, but they're not the air-tight, bulletproof coterie that their combined salaries suggest they should be. Henriquez will be coming straight off of the IL to rejoin the team in the NLDS, and Díaz, Sasaki, and Scott are all woefully unpredictable.
There is some thought that the Dodgers might carry eight relievers instead of nine, to free up a spot on the position player side for a guy like Kim. In this scenario, we'll stick with them taking nine. If not, Bubic is the most obvious cut. Last one in, first one out.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Mets should make all-out Tarik Skubal pursuit, but it could take a philosophical shift
item.dc:creator: Danny Abriano
item.description: As the Mets enter the offseason, they'll be facing a familiar challenge: put together a team that can get them back to the playoffs for the first time since 2024. David Stearns and the front office failed in that regard last offseason, due in part to the drastic changes that were made to the roster and coaching staff. There were other things at play, including long-term injuries to Francisco Lindor and Clay Holmes, some worst-case scenarios playing out, and an over-reliance on bounce backs. This
item.content:encoded:
As the Mets enter the offseason, they'll be facing a familiar challenge: put together a team that can get them back to the playoffs for the first time since 2024.
David Stearns and the front office failed in that regard last offseason, due in part to the drastic changes that were made to the roster and coaching staff. There were other things at play, including long-term injuries to Francisco Lindor and Clay Holmes, some worst-case scenarios playing out, and an over-reliance on bounce backs.
This time around, the Mets will almost certainly have much less turnover, but that doesn't mean the overall result in 2026 wasn't an abject failure.
New York had a 34-31 record after the All-Star break, which was a big improvement after things spun out of control in the first half and led to a trade deadline sell-off.
But the most important developments for the Mets after their dismal start? The emergence of Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing, the impressive return of Christian Scott, the moxie and performance of Zac Thornton, and some good late-season signs from Jonah Tong.
The above should give the Mets confidence that they're in solid shape when it comes to their lineup and a chunk of the starting rotation. They have an emerging young core to complement their more established stars, and potentially have high-upside players coming soon from the upper levels of the minors. But serious help is still needed this winter.
Specifically, the Mets need to add external help at first base, address the DH spot, bolster the bullpen with multiple new arms (including a back end option), and -- most importantly -- find a pitcher who profiles at the very top of the rotation.
In both 2025 and 2026, the Mets were done in, due in large part to not having enough starting pitching depth. And it can be argued that they left themselves short one legitimate starter both times. That can't happen again, so New York should be focused on pairing a new prospective ace with another addition who profiles in the middle or back of the rotation.
About that ace ... it's not difficult to figure out that it should be Tarik Skubal.
In one of the weakest free agent classes in recent memory, Skubal stands out even more than he ordinarily would.
Fresh off back-to-back Cy Young awards, the 29-year-old Skubal posted a 2.72 ERA (2.51 FIP) and 0.96 WHIP while walking just 1.5 per nine innings and striking out 186 batters in 158.2 innings in 2026.
Skubal's season was briefly interrupted by NanoScope surgery on his pitching elbow that kept him out of action from April 30 through June 13. But he continued to be dominant upon his return. After having a 2.70 ERA (2.11 FIP) over his first seven starts, Skubal had a 2.73 ERA (2.66 FIP) in the 19 starts he made post-surgery, with 10 of them coming after he was dealt to the Dodgers at the trade deadline.
During Stearns' end-of-season news conference on Monday at Citi Field, he was asked multiple times about the Mets' offseason plan for adding pitching, but unsurprisingly didn't offer much when asked in a roundabout way about a possible Skubal pursuit.
"I do think it is necessary for us to add to our rotation," Stearns said. "We can do that in a variety of different ways. We've talked about this plenty before -- you'd always love to add to the top of your rotation, any team would love to do that -- over the long term, what we need to do is develop pitchers at the top of our rotation, and I think we are proving we can do that, and we'll continue to do that."
While Stearns refused to make any declarations about the type of pitcher the Mets would go after, it is pointless to read into that.
For one, Skubal is still under contract with the Dodgers, and no executive is going to talk about going after a player who is on another team.
Second, and even more importantly, no exec is going to tip his or her hand entirely and risk wrecking leverage ahead of possible negotiations.
While Stearns (smartly) won't say it, I will: The Mets should make Skubal the centerpiece of their offseason plan, using the resources at their disposal to add one of the most talented pitchers in the sport to slot in front of Nolan McLean.
The Mets' biggest need this offseason is at the top of their rotation, with Skubal a nearly perfect way to fill that need. And Skubal will cost only money, since the midseason trade from Detroit to Los Angeles makes him ineligible for a qualifying offer and the draft pick compensation it would've required from any team that signed him.
When discussing Skubal and the Mets, it's obviously instructive to consider Stearns' philosophy when it comes to signing pitchers to long-term deals. Specifically, he has not shown much interest in signing pitchers in their late-20s or 30s to those kind of pacts -- and that philosophy is generally a valid one.
For every long-term, big-money deal to a pitcher 29 or older that works out (Max Scherzer's seven-year deal with the Nationals looks incredible in retrospect, and the Yankees' deal for Max Fried is aging well), you can point to a whole bunch that didn't or currently aren't (Patrick Corbin, Jacob deGrom, Jordan Zimmermann, Felix Hernandez, Corbin Burnes).
As far as how Stearns has operated in the past, it's fair to throw what he did in Milwaukee out the window given the payroll constraints he was working under.
But except for a serious pursuit of then-25-year-old Yoshinobu Yamamoto ahead of the 2024 season, Stearns' main forays into the free agent starting pitching market with the Mets have been measured:
Sean Manaea: Three years, $75 million
Clay Holmes: Three years, $38 million
Frankie Montas: Two years, $34 million
Luis Severino: One year, $13 million
Griffin Canning: One year, $4.25 million
Of those signings, Holmes was the biggest success as the Mets turned him back into a starter after he spent years in relief. But that success resulted in Holmes being set to opt out after the second season of his contract, which led to New York trading him at the deadline.
During his time leading the Mets' baseball operations, Stearns has been reluctant to offer deals to starting pitchers (except Yamamoto) that exceed three years. When that is your philosophy, the risk is obviously lower. But sometimes a calculated risk is needed.
When it comes to Skubal, there is risk. In addition to the minor surgery he had this season, Skubal underwent flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and had Tommy John surgery in 2017.
Skubal is also likely to receive the biggest deal ever for a starting pitcher when it comes to average annual value. Maybe his age (30 when next season begins) and yearly value of his deal will make the years easier to stomach, but something like $400 million for eight years is easy to imagine.
There's also the looming lockout and new CBA to consider.
While it's difficult to envision the players caving on a hard salary cap, it's fair to believe the new CBA will include stiffer penalties for teams that exceed the luxury tax thresholds.
But even after considering all of that, it's still reasonable to conclude that the Mets should go after Skubal with gusto -- that he should be the exception to Stearns' rule, maybe with a slight nudge from owner Steve Cohen.
Things could always go sideways, as they often do with long-term deals for older starting pitchers. But there's no reason to think Skubal won't be exceptional for the first half of any deal he signs, which would also theoretically line up with a World Series window the Mets will hope to be entering.
When you look at Skubal, who combines one of the best arsenals in baseball with perhaps the best command in baseball (and whose metrics look like this), the biggest risk for the Mets would be not going all-in on him.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] NLDS notes: Josue De Paula, Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman
item.dc:creator: Jacob Macofsky
item.description: While eight teams battle it out to see who will advance to the Division Series, the Dodgers are among four teams using this time off to prepare for October baseball. After winning an even 100 games in the regular season, the Dodgers secured a first-round bye and will await the winner of the NL Wild Card matchup between the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies. While the Dodgers continue to add the finishing touches to their postseason roster, there are some lingering questions as to which pl
item.content:encoded:
While eight teams battle it out to see who will advance to the Division Series, the Dodgers are among four teams using this time off to prepare for October baseball.
After winning an even 100 games in the regular season, the Dodgers secured a first-round bye and will await the winner of the NL Wild Card matchup between the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies. While the Dodgers continue to add the finishing touches to their postseason roster, there are some lingering questions as to which players will be a part of the team's depth chart.
21-year-old outfielder Josue De Paula made his presence known while filling in for the then-injured Shohei Ohtani, slashing .323/.500/.581 across 42 plate appearances before he was sent down to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sonja Chen of MLB.com believes that both De Paula and utility man Hyeseong Kim can make an impact on the postseason roster, with the former being relegated to pinch-hit opportunities due to his lack of big-league experience in the outfield.
Of course, De Paula is capable of playing the corner outfield, but we only saw him play six innings in left as a Dodger. And given how important defense is in the postseason, I doubt we will see him in the field unless it's an emergency.
The month of September has given Shohei Ohtani plenty of time to prepare for his third consecutive postseason run with the Dodgers. The Dodgers still have another three days to prepare for the NLDS, and Ohtani is using this time to get his swing in the right place, per Chen.
"Everything is feeling great physically," general manager Brandon Gomes said on a Zoom call with the media on Tuesday. "The swings, once he came back, overall were in a good place. And using these five days to continue to get reps and feeling good into this series is really important. But feels like he's in a great spot."
Freddie Freeman had his power zapped in the second half of the regular season, hitting just one home run while posting a slugging percentage of .339. Freeman dealt with patellar tendonitis in his right knee, but entering the NLDS, he said that he's feeling a lot better, reports Jack Harris of the California Post.
"I truly feel good right now, physically," Freeman said on Tuesday, during a video conference with reporters ahead of the Dodgers' first pre-National League Division Series bye week workout. "So it's on me now to figure out the mechanics of the swing in the next five days. And I have all the confidence in myself that I will figure that out by [Game 1 on] Saturday."

item.content:encoded:
【ロサンゼルス29日（日本時間30日）＝横山尚杜】米大リーグ、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手（32）が10月3日（同4日）に開幕する地区シリーズ（5回戦制）に向け、全体練習に参加。球団が公開した練習の様子では屋外フリー打撃を実施する姿があった。「右上腕二頭筋の炎症」で負傷者リスト（IL）入りして以降、初めて取材対応したロバーツ監督、球団編成は口をそろえて「状態はいい」と大谷のコンディションに自信を見せた。
報道陣非公開で行われたドジャースタジアムでの全体練習。シーズン終了からわずか1日の休養を経て、ワールドシリーズ3連覇を狙うチームが再始動した。球団は大谷が、屋外フリーを実施する練習風景を投稿。「ウッ！」と声が漏れるほどのフルスイングを見せ、同僚と比較しても打球音は際立っていた。
「この2カ月で、最もいい状態のショウヘイを見ることができると思う。自信があるよ。彼が打線にいるだけで脅威になるが、パフォーマンスという面でも期待しているモノを見せてくれる」
ロバーツ監督はオンラインで取材対応し、地区シリーズまでに大谷の状態がさらに上向くことに疑いがなかった。「右上腕二頭筋の炎症」による負傷者リスト（IL）から復帰後、5試合の出場で21打数5安打8三振。実戦勘を含めると万全とは言えず、コンディションに懸念を持たせるスイングもあった。ただ、指揮官によると「トレーニングスタッフからの報告も、日に日に良くなっている」という。
地区シリーズの開幕まで中5日の期間が空くが、ドジャースの休養は1日だけ。チームには大谷が移籍1年目だった24年の成功体験がある。実戦勘、緊張感、熱量を落とさず、多くの時間を過ごすことで一体感を高める。同年にも実施したワイルドカードシリーズを観戦する「ウオッチパーティー」を開催し、球場の興奮に心身を慣らす。22、23年はシーズンで100勝以上を挙げるも、地区シリーズで敗退。その反省を生かしたプランで、強豪は休養日の過ごし方も熟知している。
ドジャースは故障者が少なく、ほぼフルメンバーが揃う。大谷と右膝に違和感を抱えるフリーマンの状態が数少ない不透明な要素だ。ただ、ポストシーズンの勝負所で結果を残せば、それまでの不振も懸念も全て吹き飛ぶ。

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers to get ‘huge impact’ with key reliever on track for NLDS return
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Over the last two months of the regular season, no team had a more productive bullpen than the Dodgers. And come the start of their postseason trek on Saturday, the team might be adding another key arm back to the group. General manager Brandon Gomes announced on Tuesday that the club expects to have hard-throwing right-handed reliever Edgardo Henriquez available for its National League Division Series, an encouraging development after Henriquez missed the final couple weeks of the regular seaso
item.content:encoded:
Over the last two months of the regular season, no team had a more productive bullpen than the Dodgers.
And come the start of their postseason trek on Saturday, the team might be adding another key arm back to the group.
General manager Brandon Gomes announced on Tuesday that the club expects to have hard-throwing right-handed reliever Edgardo Henriquez available for its National League Division Series, an encouraging development after Henriquez missed the final couple weeks of the regular season with a strain in his back.
Prior to getting hurt, Henriquez was emerging as one of the top arms in the Dodgers’ resurgent relief corps (which led all MLB bullpens in August and September with 4.3 combined wins above replacement, according to Fangraphs, and ranked fourth in that stretch in combined ERA at 3.20).
A 24-year-old former prospect who has started to routinely eclipse 103 mph with his fastball, Henriquez ranked fourth among the team’s relievers (minimum 20 appearances) with a 2.85 ERA this season. He also struck out 70 batters in 60 total innings and converted each of the ninth-inning save opportunities he received.
Henriquez had hit his stride in August and early September, allowing just one run in a 17-game stretch that featured 25 strikeouts and only two walks and seven hits allowed.
However, after giving up two runs in a Sept. 13 appearance in Miami against the Marlins, he went on the IL with his back injury –– one that initially cast doubt on his postseason availability.
Luckily for the Dodgers, Henriquez’s status has improved since then. He resumed a throwing during the team’s final regular-season homestand. He recently completed a session of live batting practice without feeling any lingering discomfort. And while Gomes said “we still got a few steps to go” before Henriquez gets the green light to return, every indication is that he should be available for the club’s best-of-five NLDS.
“If that all goes well, then yeah, the expectation is he’ll be on the roster,” Gomes said.
“Given the body of work, what he’s done, the unique skill set, that could be huge for us,” manager Dave Roberts added, before correcting himself: “Will be huge for us.”
Indeed, Henriquez would figure to occupy a high-leverage spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen. He gives them not only a trustworthy right-hander option –– along with Roki Sasaki, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart and the recently resurgent Edwin Díaz –– but also one of the biggest fastballs in the game.
Henriquez’s 100.7 mph average fastball velocity ranked second among MLB pitchers this season, behind only star Padres closer Mason Miller. The team’s next-hardest thrower is Sasaki, whose heater averaged only 97.9 mph this year (though could increase in the playoffs as he shifts to a bullpen role).
Last October, Henriquez was a mixed bag in the playoffs. In two of his appearances (Game 1 of the wild card series and Game 5 of the World Series), he failed to record an out while allowing a hit and two walks in both outings. But in the other (Game 3 of the World Series), he pitched two scoreless frames in the team’s marathon 18-inning win, becoming an unsung hero in their Fall Classic triumph.
This time, Henriquez is set for a prominent role, assuming he gets through one more session of live batting practice OK.
“[He would make a] huge impact,” Roberts said. “I think he’s one of those guys that getting the bye has really benefited.”

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Freddie Freeman Reveals Injury Status Ahead of Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman has been dealing with knee pain toward the end of this season, but the Boys in Blue securing a bye for the Wild Card round may be his saving grace. Freeman said Tuesday that he feels better than he had recently, with “no pain in my knee right now.” He added that he’s using this period of five days without games to get some “mental rest,” though his physical preparation for the playoffs is far from over. Freddie Freeman making changes ahead of pla
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman has been dealing with knee pain toward the end of this season, but the Boys in Blue securing a bye for the Wild Card round may be his saving grace.
Freeman said Tuesday that he feels better than he had recently, with “no pain in my knee right now.”
He added that he’s using this period of five days without games to get some “mental rest,” though his physical preparation for the playoffs is far from over.
Freddie Freeman making changes ahead of playoffs
Freeman, who according to ESPN hit a dreadful .184/.259/.224 in September after a roaring summer at the plate, said he’s making some changes this week.
In particular, he’s looking at his swing and how to get back on track this October.
Freeman said “I’ll be hitting BP every day” and is working a plan he has on how to make himself a dangerous hitter again when October comes around.
After all, in June, he slashed .337/.425/.548/.973, and he followed that up with a torrid July as well, hitting .348/.384/.467/.851.
Freeman said in October 2024, he felt “probably 100 times worse,” so he think he can figure it out for this postseason, too.
“I have all the confidence in myself that I will figure it out by Saturday,” he said.
Freddie Freeman sounds off on Dodgers’ mindset ahead of playoffs
Freeman also faced the inevitable questions about this team’s quest for a third straight title, something he said he’s “personally not thinking about.”
Instead, Freeman said he’s keeping his focus on this upcoming series, including who the Dodgers will play and how to beat them.
“I think if you think big picture in this moment, you’re going to lose you lose sight of some things,” he said. “You just got to take each day one at one day at a time. And we do understand the bigger picture, but if you’re looking at the bigger picture, the you won’t be able to get to that big picture if you’re not focusing on the now.”
It sounds like Freeman and the rest of the Dodgers are locked in on this weekend.
Do you think the Dodgers will three-peat this season?

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Expect Edgardo Henriquez Back for NLDS If Final Tests Go Well
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers reliever Edgardo Henriquez is “trending really well,” according to general manager Brandon Gomes, and he is looking likely to be on the NLDS roster.
Henriquez is still on the injured list with a lower back injury, which shut him down for the last two weeks of the regular season.
Edgardo Henriquez injury status
When speaking to the media, including Dodgers Nation, on Tuesday, September 29th, Gomes said Henriquez threw a live batting practice session against hitters, and it went well.
Henriquez also has additional activities lined up during the bye week to clear up, including simulated games and more live batting sessions.
If he clears the remaining checkmarks, Henriquez will be ready for the NLDS, per Gomes.
“We’ve still got a few steps to go, but if all that goes well, the expectation is he will be on the roster,” the general manager said.
What will Henriquez’s role be with the bullpen?
Before he got hurt, Henriquez was a set-up man for the Dodgers, and he was also a budding closer for the team thanks to his consistency.
Tanner Scott is prone to home runs, while Edwin Diaz was in a spiral, which helped Henriquez emerge as the most consistent relief pitcher.
Over the last few weeks, Scott has been steady, while Diaz has rebuilt himself from the ground up. Additionally, Roki Sasaki moved into the bullpen, leading the Dodgers into the postseason with plenty of candidates to close, Henriquez among them.
“Obviously we’ve had a lot of talent over the years,” manager Dave Roberts said. “But as far as sitting here today at the end of the season, it’s as good of shape as we’ve ever been in with the bullpen.
“That could change in a day, in a game, as we all know. But right now, feel really good about everyone out there.”
Roberts is known for making bullpen decisions based on feel in the postseason, and depending on how Henriquez looks coming back, he may close or perhaps settle into a middle relief role.
Luckily, the Dodgers have bullpen options, which hasn’t been the case for a while.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers rattled the MLB world after they acquired southpaw Tarik Skubal back in August.
He is currently under a one-year, $32 million contract with the Dodgers, but he is heading toward free agency.
Former general manager Jim Duquette has revealed his price tag prediction and linked him to Los Angeles.
Dodgers Could Retain Skubal for a Massive Price
Skubal’s future is one of the most pressing subjects across the major leagues right now.
According to Duquette, per SNY Mets, the 29-year-old could be facing a $400 million deal with Los Angeles.
“I do think that it gets to $400 (million),” he said. “I think it’ll be the Dodgers and I do think it’ll be the Mets. Those are the two teams that will be most interested and most able to afford him.”
At the time of this writing, Skubal has a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts across 158.2 innings pitched through 26 starts. He’s walked 27 batters.
This marks his seventh season playing Major League Baseball, but only his first with an organization other than the Detroit Tigers.
The Tigers selected him 255th overall in the ninth round of the 2018 MLB draft. He made his debut in August 2020.
Hearing Duquette name such a price isn’t too surprising — it’s known that Skubal’s future is going to be an expensive one.
As noted by Jeff Passan of ESPN earlier this month, “The number will be huge. Bear in mind that Skubal turns 30 in November and never before has a pitcher age 30 or older received more than Stephen Strasburg’s $245 million (on a seven-year deal) in free agency. Provided there is no salary cap, Skubal could get double that.”
Passan predicts the deal would be for “at least a decade.”
Skubal is presumably a favorite to remain with the Dodgers — shipping out would once again shake the big leagues.
Where the Dodgers Stand Right Now Ahead of NLDS
The Wild Card Series is in full swing, but Los Angeles has already cinched its spot in the National League Division Series.
Game 1 is scheduled for Saturday, Oct. 3, at Dodger Stadium, kicking off the best-of-five series.
They will either face the Philadelphia Phillies or the Atlanta Braves, depending on who secures the victory in the Wild Card Series.
Los Angeles has a 100-62 overall record. The only team with a stronger record is the Milwaukee Brewers (103-59).
If the Dodgers pull off an NLDS win, they will advance to the NLCS for a best-of-seven series in hopes of reaching the prestigious World Series.
They have a glaring opportunity to clinch their third consecutive World Series title.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Max Muncy Reveals the Dodgers' Strategy to 'Keep the Switch Flipped' for October
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: Max Muncy is no stranger to postseason baseball, but he said it still fires him up. The longtime Los Angeles Dodger returned to his All-Star form this season, but he knows October is where you prove your worth. On Tuesday, he revealed what he and the team are doing to prepare for a run at a third straight World Series title. What are the Dodgers doing to get ready for the playoffs? As the Dodgers wait to find out who they’ll be facing in the National League Division Series, the players are worki
item.content:encoded:
Max Muncy is no stranger to postseason baseball, but he said it still fires him up.
The longtime Los Angeles Dodger returned to his All-Star form this season, but he knows October is where you prove your worth.
On Tuesday, he revealed what he and the team are doing to prepare for a run at a third straight World Series title.
What are the Dodgers doing to get ready for the playoffs?
As the Dodgers wait to find out who they’ll be facing in the National League Division Series, the players are working to stay ready and are strengthening their bond ahead of a grueling October.
“We’re trying to focus on ourselves getting ready this week,” he said via Zoom.
The way Muncy described the team’s strategy was something akin to the saying “if you stay ready, you don’t have to get ready.”
Similar to what the team did in 2024, the Dodgers still gather at the stadium daily, even without games to play.
It comes at a cost to players’ personal lives and time with their families, but Muncy argued that it’s necessary for the nature of playoff baseball.
Whereas teams with a bye might be more rested, they also are “going to be facing a team that’s already been through the fire.”
“It’s hard to go from being in an at-home setting to find trying to find a way to flip the switch,” he said. “And so the best way for us to do that was you get everyone together, you keep them at the field, you find a way to not let that switch ever be flipped off. That was something that I thought we did a really good job of in ’24 and we’re going to try to do it again this year.”
It also helps the Dodgers continue to build team chemistry, as “the postseason is when you’re going to come together,” he said.
That cohesiveness will be key when the level of competition is this high.
Dodgers expect to get everyone’s best
The Dodgers have struggled against some of the top teams in baseball this year, but Muncy said every opponent is difficult.
“This is the big leagues. These are the best players in the world,” he said.
Given that, he’s not worried about the level of competition changing in the playoffs, pointing to multiple examples of one team dominating another in the regular season only for the tables to be flipped come October.
“I know there’s things you look at on paper where you say, ‘this is a good matchup,’ but in October, it really doesn’t matter,” he said.
All that does matter is what happens on the field, and on Saturday, we’ll find out.
Do you like Max Muncy’s mindset heading into the playoffs?

item.title: [si.com] The Potentially Fatal Flaw For Each MLB Playoff Team
item.dc:creator: Ryan Phillips
item.description: The MLB playoffs are here as 12 teams survived the regular season and are ready for an all-out battle for October supremacy. Each of the remaining squads has spent the last six months proving it belonged in the postseason. None of the last teams standing got here unscathed and all have glaring weaknesses that could end their seasons early. With postseason baseball upon us, here is the fatal flaw that could derail each MLB playoff team. Brewers: Lack of Power The Brewers were baseball’s best team
item.content:encoded:
The MLB playoffs are here as 12 teams survived the regular season and are ready for an all-out battle for October supremacy. Each of the remaining squads has spent the last six months proving it belonged in the postseason. None of the last teams standing got here unscathed and all have glaring weaknesses that could end their seasons early.
With postseason baseball upon us, here is the fatal flaw that could derail each MLB playoff team.
Brewers: Lack of Power
The Brewers were baseball’s best team all season but that doesn’t mean they’re perfect. Milwaukee has a great rotation fronted by baseball’s new ace Jacob Misiorowski, and a good bullpen, but the lineup relies heavily on getting hits up and down the lineup. The Brewers play the 2026 version of small ball, and don’t have a ton of power. That can kill teams in October, when runs come at a premium.
Milwaukee finished the season tied for 28th in home runs (154) and 25th in isolated power (.144). The Brewers were tied for 10th in slugging (.403) and were third in wRC+ (107), but the lack of top-line power could be their downfall. Against elite pitching in the postseason, it’s much more difficult to string together hits and build big innings. Being able to get runs on balls that leave the yard is huge. Each of the last six World Series champions ranked inside the top five in regular season home runs.
Maybe Milwaukee bucks that trend, but if they don’t win the World Series, a lack of power may be the reason.
Dodgers: Health
The Dodgers have won two straight titles and at full strength, they’d be the overwhelming favorite to take home a third in a row. But L.A. has dealt with major injuries all season and the team looks more vulnerable than it has in a long time as we enter the postseason.
Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow combined to make only 22 starts this season. Both are back now, but neither has been particularly reliable—Snell left his penultimate start on Sept. 16 with a groin injury before returning to pitch four innings on Saturday. Tarik Skubal had elbow surgery earlier this year with the Tigers and hasn’t been quite as dominant as usual when it comes to limiting baserunners. Shohei Ohtani has been sidelined by knee and biceps injuries, and won’t be pitching in October. Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts and Teoscar Hernandez are showing signs of decline and have played a ton of baseball over the last three years.
L.A. is still loaded, but a few injuries to a roster that’s had its fair share of medical issues could make things dicey.
Rays: Trouble Against Lefties
It’s hard to find too many flaws here. The Rays are an incredibly balanced squad that was the best in the AL pretty much all season. One of the only red flags here is the team’s performance against lefties, and they’re likely to run into a few in the playoffs.
Against lefties as a team, Tampa Bay ranked 27th in slugging (.364), 26th in wRC+ (90) and 25th in OPS (.679). Luckily for the Rays, their best offensive players hammered lefties. Junior Caminero slashed .287/.426/.490 with eight home runs and a 152 wRC+. Unfortunately, the 23-year-old and Yandy Diaz are the team’s only players who appeared in 100-plus games and topped .700 in OPS against lefties.
That’s a weakness opponents will try to exploit in October. The Rays don’t have many holes, but good left-handed pitching could be the kryptonite that slows one of baseball’s most complete teams.
Braves: A Hole at Shortstop
The Braves have plenty of star power in the lineup and Chris Sale at the top of their rotation but they have a huge flaw at the heart of their team. Atlanta’s shortstops were among the worst offensively during the 2026 season. Ha-seong Kim is is the starter, but he had a .359 OPS with zero home runs in 147 plate appearances this season so I’m not sure that is the answer. The other option is Mauricio Dubón, who had a .719 OPS in 153 games, but that won’t work against southpaws since it means lefty Mike Yastrzemski must play left field.
Collectively, Braves shortstops slashed .241/.295/.349 during the regular season and ranked 27th with a wRC+ of 78. They also ranked 23rd in fWAR (1.6) and bWAR (-0.4). They simply haven’t gotten enough out of the position and need to find some offensive production there.
Atlanta went wire-to-wire to win the NL East and did so while not getting much from a premium position. Against elite pitching in the postseason, they’ll need production out of everyone in the lineup at some point. Carrying an empty spot will likely prove to be more damaging than it already has been.
Yankees: An Aaron Judge-Sized Hole in the Lineup
The Yankees may have baseball’s best postseason rotation and found enough offense to hold onto the AL’s top wild-card spot. But to win a World Series, they need their best player healthy and hammering baseballs. They may not have it.
Aaron Judge is trying to return for the wild-card series from a strained calf muscle, but it would be unwise to rush him back into action. Yes, New York needs his bat in the lineup, but it also needs to ensure he is available for the entire postseason, not just the first series. Ben Rice (149), Cody Bellinger (115) and Paul Goldschmidt (111) are the only Yankees with more than 300 plate appearances and a wRC+ over 100. That’s a scary lack of production from the lineup.
They need Judge’s bat back at full health as soon as possible simply because the team relies on him so much to produce.
Padres: Who Starts After Michael King?
The Padres have baseball’s best bullpen and an offense that has been clicking on all cylinders in the second half. What they don’t have is a deep rotation after injuries have decimated it.
Michael King is the team’s ace and should be reliable in that spot, but after him things get dicey. Nick Pivetta missed most of the season due to a flexor strain in his pitching elbow that cost him nearly five months. He’s back and has thrown well, but he’s only made eight starts this year. After that, it’ll be some combination of Robbie Ray and Walker Buehler. Both have been up and down this season and neither feels like a rock-solid option.
If San Diego can get decent starts and shorten games by getting the bullpen in early, things could be fine. But if the team’s starters struggle it could mean an early exit.
Cubs: A Battered Starting Rotation
The Cubs have one of baseball’s best offenses and its best all-around player in Pete Crow-Armstrong, but their pitching staff remains a patchwork mess. The team’s starting rotation has endured season-ending injuries to Cade Horton and Ben Brown, Justin Steele still hasn’t returned after elbow surgery in 2025, Matthew Boyd missed time thanks to knee surgery and a shoulder issue, and Kevin Gausman is now dealing with a shoulder injury.
Chicago will open the postseason with Boyd on the mound and should follow with Clay Holmes in Game 2, then Shota Imanaga and, if he’s healthy enough, Gausman. How bad has it been for the Cubs? Among starters, only Imanaga generated 2.0 bWAR this year. That’s a dangerous weakness to carry into the postseason when pitching becomes even more important.
Could the Cubs manage to overcome a rotation that has been battered all season? It’s possible, but that would take a herculean effort from the team’s top-ranked offense.
Phillies: Trea Turner’s Disappearing Production
Trea Turner was a key piece of the Phillies’ success in 2025, as he slashed .302/.354/.450 with 15 home runs, 36 stolen bases and a 123 wRC+ in 141 games. The team is probably wondering where that guy went.
In 157 games this year, Turner slashed .242/.297/.378 with 19 home runs, 21 stolen bases and a wRC+ of 83. His strikeout rate jumped from 16.7% to 21.0%, his xBA dropped from .270 to .242 and his xwOBA of .293 ranked in the 14th percentile. That would be manageable if Turner provided value defensively, but his outs above average dropped from 17 in 2025 to -8 this season. That’s a precipitous, ominous drop for a shortstop who’s in his age-33 season, has always depended on his athleticism and still has seven more years on his contract. Philadelphia has underachieved as a whole in 2026, and Turner is the poster child.
While he was a disappointment in the regular season, Turner has a ton of playoff experience and won a title with the Nationals in 2019. Maybe he’ll turn it around when the lights are the brightest. But his postseason track record doesn’t offer much optimism. He has a career playoff OPS of .681.
Red Sox: A Top-Heavy Offense
Boston’s comeback story this season was remarkable after Alex Cora was fired following a 10–17 start. While they were one of MLB’s best teams over the final two-thirds of the season, the offense never really clicked one through nine. As a team, the Red Sox finished 17th in wRC+ (99) and 19th in OPS (.717). And it seemed all season a few guys would come through, while the rest of the lineup struggled.
Among the team’s hitters who played at least 100 games, only Willson Contreras (151), Wilyer Abreu (112) and Ceddanne Rafaela (109) topped 100 in wRC+ to grade out as above-average hitters. The drop-off from Contreras to the rest of the roster is pretty alarming in itself, though Mickey Gasper (130), Masataka Yoshida (108) and Roman Anthony (106) all performed well in fewer than 300 plate appearances. Key pieces like Caleb Durbin (100) and especially Jarren Duran (69) had off years, while catcher Adley Rutschman slashed .222/.278/.410 with a wRC+ of 88 after arriving at the trade deadline.
Boston will have to overcome those issues throughout the lineup, particularly against the kind of pitching ahead in the postseason. The lack of offensive balance could be the team’s downfall.
Guardians: A Lineup Short of Firepower
The Guardians are in an enviable position, as they barely made the playoffs but wound up with the AL’s No. 2 seed. While they are set up for success thanks to the bracket and have an excellent pitching staff, their lineup has been anemic.
Cleveland finished the regular season ranked 27th in home runs (162) and slugging (.380), 26th in OPS (.696), 24th in runs scored (678) and 21st in wRC+ (97). Meanwhile, star third baseman José Ramírez wrapped up the worst full season of his career, slashing .235/.320/.368 with 12 home runs and a wRC+ of 92. The question is simple: Where do the runs come from? Rookie Chase DeLauter was the team’s most productive hitter after slashing .287/.363/.456 with 16 home runs and a 131 wRC+, but he doesn't have much help. Steven Kwan was second on the team in wRC+ (114), but only slugged .349, while Travis Bazzana (110) and Angel Martinez (108) were both only modestly above average by wRC+. The rest of the lineup struggled to generate offense.
After a tough battle down the stretch, the Guardians wound up with a favorable path in the postseason. But getting to the World Series will likely require unearthing some unsung heroes on offense.
White Sox: October Inexperience
The White Sox surprised everyone with their run to a postseason berth after three consecutive 100-loss seasons. The roster has been properly overhauled, with only 19.8% of the team’s plate appearances coming from players on the 121-loss team in 2024. The problem is, most of the team’s new players have little to no postseason experience.
Braden Montgomery, Munetaka Murakami and Sam Antonacci are rookies, while Colson Montgomery, Kyle Teel, Chase Meidroth and Grant Taylor are second-year players. Sean Burke debuted in 2024, but has never pitched in the postseason, and All-Star Miguel Vargas has likewise never appeared in the postseason despite coming up with the Dodgers. Maybe there’s something to be said for youthful exuberance, but there’s also the possibility that fatigue becomes a factor for players who haven’t been through a playoff chase before. Colson Montgomery posted a wRC+ of 54 after August 1, while Murakami slashed .156/.299/.375 in that stretch.
Chicago is built for success long-term, but its lack of postseason experience could be a significant obstacle in October.
Astros: A Thin Starting Rotation
The Astros finished 81–81 to win the weak AL West and notch a playoff spot. Given their record, it’s not surprising they have a ton of issues across the roster. The most glaring is their starting rotation, which is in rough shape.
Beyond Hunter Brown, Houston simply doesn’t have the kind of high-end starting pitching that wins in October. And even Brown enters the playoffs with some uncertainty, having thrown only 107 ⅓ innings this season after missing a chunk of the campaign with a shoulder injury. Peter Lambert has become the team’s No. 2 starter, but he went 8–10 with a 3.82 ERA and doesn’t possess premium stuff. Hayden Wesneski finished the season strong, but made only 11 starts all year, while Cristian Javier and Mike Burrows are both on the IL.
The rotation is so thin that the Astros are poised to open Game 1 of the wild-card series with a bullpen game to give Brown, Lambert and Wesneski rest. It’s hardly an ideal situation and there aren’t many options available for manager Joe Espada.
Ryan Phillips is a senior writer on the Breaking and Trending News team at Sports Illustrated. He has worked in digital media since 2009, spending eight years at The Big Lead before joining SI in 2024. Phillips also co-hosts The Assembly Call Podcast about Indiana Hoosiers basketball and previously worked at Bleacher Report. He is a proud San Diego native and a graduate of Indiana University’s journalism program.
Follow rumorsandrants

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Mets-Tarik Skubal rumors have already begun before Dodgers' playoff run has even started
item.dc:creator: Drew Koch
item.description: The MLB Postseason officially gets underway on Tuesday, but the Los Angeles Dodgers won't take the field until later this weekend thanks to their 100-62 record and a first-round bye. item.content:encoded:
The MLB Postseason officially gets underway on Tuesday, but the Los Angeles Dodgers won't take the field until later this weekend thanks to their 100-62 record and a first-round bye. Dodgers' manager Dave Roberts now has plenty of time to set his rotation for the upcoming NLDS matchup; one that will almost certainly feature Tarik Skubal as LA's starter for Game 1 or 2.
But it would seem that the New York Mets already have their sights set on the Dodgers' free agent to-be. Will Sammon of The Athletic claims that Skubal to the Mets makes a lot of sense on paper, but stopped short of calling it no-brainer thanks in large part to the upcoming labor negotiations.
Dodgers & Mets look to be Tarik Skubal's most likely free agent suitors
Sammon cites the potential for a salary cap and the exorbitant salaries already on the Mets books — namely Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor — as the two biggest obstacles that could put a halt to New York's pursuit of Skubal. Those same barriers could force the Dodgers to hit the pause button as well. LA has a ton of hefty, long-term contracts that would impact the club if a salary cap was implemented.
Few, if any, know how the upcoming negotiations between the owners and the Player's Association are going to play out, but the economic impact and how teams could be required to spend in the future could greatly alter who pursues Skubal this winter and how much they'll be willing to offer.
Then there's the other aspect that no one is really talking about — at least not yet. The negotiating window will be extremely short. With the Collective Bargaining Agreement set to expire on December 1, teams will have a little more than three weeks to lay the groundwork for a potential landmark contract with the two-time Cy Young award-winner.
Throw in the fact that he's represented by Scott Boras — baseball's super-agent who's known for extending these negotiations well into the springtime — and the likelihood of striking a deal before the window closes looks less and less by the day. Yet, the potential salary cap, and thereby reduction in salary, could be enough to prompt Boras and Skubal to get a new deal done posthaste.
Much like the Mets, the Dodgers will undoubtedly be interested in re-signing Skubal this winter. Frankly, it may be a two-team race to determine who'll walk away with the offseason biggest prize. Few other organizations have the resources to ink the southpaw to the record-breaking deal he'll surely be seeking. Most pundits expect the deal to be worth more than $400 million.

item.content:encoded:
JustPredictions
Justice editors predict the upcoming year of sports.
Ben Khayat ’28: Only one Big Ten team will make the College Football Playoffs. The sample size is small, but the Big Ten has been downright shameful to start the 2026 season. The obvious examples are the Michigan Wolverines coming back from the dead to prevent a home loss to the Western Michigan Broncos, and the Rutgers Scarlet Knights succumbing to the UMass Minutemen, a team that didn’t win a single game last season. The rest of the conference hasn’t been much better. The Oregon Ducks came into the season ranked #2 in the country, but came up limping in their one-score win over the Boise State Broncos before getting dispatched by Oklahoma State on Saturday. The Ohio State Buckeyes led 23-3 against the Texas Longhorns, only to allow 21 unanswered points and choke what would have been the first statement win the conference has had this season. Come January, I can’t imagine many of these “top” teams will have impressed anybody enough to get an at-large bid over some other power conference opponents.
Luca D. Jordan ’28: The Chicago Bears will make the Superbowl this season. After having an amazing breakout season under head coach Ben Johnson and making their first playoff appearance since 2020, the Chicago Bears have shown explosive growth with a new offensive direction. Defined by their comeback wins, the Bears almost clinched the semi-finals last season, but quarterback Caleb Williams threw a bad pass that led to an interception against the Los Angeles Rams. Despite an unfortunate play that ended his season early, Williams has shown flashes of an all time great quarterback. When it comes down to the last few seconds, Williams is known to perform herculean throws to save the game. Although their offseason wasn’t particularly exciting, expect a surprising surge in performance across the board from the entire roster. Previous champs Seattle Seahawks are dead in the water without Sam Darnold and the Rams have added some big names to their roster, but it’s just stars over substance. The Bears have a few decades of an underdog legacy behind them, and that’s too much destiny to ignore.
Bryan Wolfe ’27: The New York Knicks are running it back! I have faith. Even though the Philadelphia 76ers have the starting five of doom and despair, I believe in the king of New York Jalen Brunson to lead us back to the promised land.
Chava Thiell ’29: Alexander Zverev will finish the 2026 ATP season with an ATP finals win and the World #1 ranking. As unfortunate as it may be for diehard Sincaraz fans, Jannik Sinner isn’t healthy and Carlos Alcaraz is still adjusting to his return to tennis after a four-month hiatus. After Zverev clinched two Slams this year, his momentum cannot seem to be stopped. Conversely, I think Aryba Sabalenka will walk away with the WTA Finals trophy, inspired by a heartbreaking US Open final loss to rival Elena Rybakina and a mission to come away from the season with a big tournament win.
Eli Sandalow ’28: The New England Patriots will go 4-13. Drake Maye looks like he regressed, AJ Brown is prone to long-term injuries and Rhamondre Stevenson is one of the most overrated running backs in the NFL right now.
Alyssa Wu ‘29: The Dodgers won’t three-peat this year.The Dodgers have a stacked lineup, with Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and Mookie Betts, plus a star-studded starting rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. Along with their veterans, new acquisitions this year include stars like Tarik Skubal, a two-time American League Cy Young winner. Despite this, the Dodgers have not dominated through the season as many expected. They went 13-14 in August, though they have found their footing again in September. Injuries raise more concerns; Ohtani only returned to the lineup on September 23 after a stint on the injured list and is not expected to pitch for the remainder of the season. Reliever Blake Treinen, who has helped bring three championships to the Dodgers in his six seasons, suffered a season-ending injury on September 26. With Kyle Tucker and Andy Pages being the only starting position players under the age of 30, the question is whether these Dodger veterans will be healthy and as productive as they used to be during the postseason. The MLB Playoff bracket itself does not always reward the ‘best’ team. The Dodgers in 2022 are one of the clearest examples of this. In 2022, they went 111-51 and won 14 of 19 regular-season games against the Padres. However, after winning Game 1 of the NLDS, they lost three straight to the San Diego Padres, ending their season. The postseason can bring plenty of surprises, and a team’s regular season does not always predict its success in the playoffs. The Dodgers had to come back from a 3-2 deficit to win last year’s World Series, and this year’s team seems to be much more vulnerable. The Dodgers are sure to make it far in the playoffs, but another championship is far from guaranteed.

item.content:encoded:
Eight Dodgers on Monday were nominated for Major League Baseball’s All-MLB teams, an honor that has existed within the sport since 2019.
Fan voting for the honor will take place beginning Monday through Friday, October 9, with that fan vote counted alongside “a decorated panel of media members, broadcasters, former players and other officials throughout the game” in determining first and second All-MLB teams.
Shohei Ohtani is one of six nominees at designated hitter, Mookie Betts is one of 11 shortstop nominees, and Freddie Freeman one of 14 nominees at first base. All five have captured All-MLB honors in five previous years, with Ohtani collecting first-team All-MLB honors at DH in each of the last three years and four of the last five, plus second-team DH in 2022, to go with his two first-team All-MLB honors (2022-23) and one second-team All-MLB honors (2021) as a starting pitcher.
Betts is a four-time first-team All-MLB outfielder plus a second-team honor in 2019. Freeman has two first-team honors at first base, the last coming in 2023, and three second-team honors.
Max Muncy is one of 11 third baseman vying for All-MLB honors, looking for his first All-MLB selection, facing an uphill battle with Rays star Junior Caminero among those nominated at the position.
Andy Pages is the only Dodger among the 24 outfield nominees, seeking his first All-MLB selection.’
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who garnered first-team All-MLB honors last year, and Tarik Skubal, a first-teamer in each of the last two years, are the two Dodgers starting pitchers nominated at starting pitcher this year.
Tanner Scott is one of 20 relief pitchers up for All-MLB honors.
All-MLB teams will be announced during the MLB awards show on November 11, which will begin at 5 p.m. PT on MLB Network.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Locked in as No. 2 seed, Dodgers turn to Tarik Skubal vs. Giants
item.description: Having seen their chances of gaining the top seed in the National League playoffs die in a two-game span, the Los Angeles Dodgers get an opportunity to coast into the postseason when they open a three-game road set against the San Francisco Giants on Friday. He will be opposed by Giants right-hander Yunior Marte (0-1, 4.66). While they can’t overtake the Milwau
item.content:encoded:
Having seen their chances of gaining the top seed in the National League playoffs die in a two-game span, the Los Angeles Dodgers get an opportunity to coast into the postseason when they open a three-game road set against the San Francisco Giants on Friday.
Left-hander Tarik Skubal (11-7, 2.85 ERA) is scheduled to get his final tune-up for the postseason in the series opener for the Dodgers. He will be opposed by Giants right-hander Yunior Marte (0-1, 4.66).
While they can’t overtake the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record, the Dodgers (97-62) have clinched the NL West title and the second-best record in the league. The latter will earn them a first-round bye in the playoffs, meaning after Sunday’s regular-season finale in San Francisco, they won’t play again until next Saturday.
Skubal will be making his 10th start since he was acquired from the Detroit Tigers at the trade deadline. Los Angeles has won seven of his nine outings, including the last six.
Skubal wasn’t particularly effective in a five-inning start against the Giants last Saturday in which he allowed four runs, two on a home run by Victor Bericoto. The Dodgers supported him with seven runs in those five innings, allowing him to walk away with a win.
He has faced the Giants just three times in his career, going 2-1 with a 4.30 ERA.
Skubal should have additional firepower supporting him in the rematch as the Dodgers have brought Shohei Ohtani and Andy Pages back from injuries over the last three days.
Each got extensive playing time in the just-completed home series against the Padres, with Pages playing in all three games and Ohtani the last two, each going 3-for-9.
Both are expected to play significantly against the Giants, with the team getting five days off to start next week.
“I think we all know why it’s important,” Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman said about the importance of the first-round bye. “There’s a lot of us kind of limping toward the end here. It’s good to get those guys (Ohtani and Pages) back on the field, get some ABs in them and then rest up.”
Skubal will be matched up once again with Marte, who allowed six runs in 4 2/3 innings in the meeting in Los Angeles last week. A rookie facing the Dodgers for the first time, he served up a home run to Will Smith in taking the loss in his fourth major league appearance.
The Dodgers could see a familiar face late in the game with the Giants on Thursday having claimed their former closer, Camilo Doval, on waivers from the Pirates.
After 4 1/2 seasons in San Francisco in which he recorded 107 saves and was an All-Star in 2023, the Giants sent Doval to the New York Yankees last July for four prospects. One year and one day later, the Yankees flipped the right-hander to Pittsburgh, which in turn saw him pitch just 20 times before cutting him loose, allowing the Giants to snatch him back.
Interestingly, should Doval or another newcomer — catcher Zach Morgan — get into a game during the Dodgers series, the Giants (65-94) would tie the major-league record for number of players used in a season with 71. Should they both play, they would break the record.
Giants manager Tony Vitello joked to reporters Wednesday about the possibility of setting the record.
“I guess, you know, being the first year in the organization, you’d like to get to meet everybody,” he said. “So this is one way to do it.”
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
復帰後の成績は「21打数5安打、打率.238、8三振」だが…
MLBレギュラーシーズンは現地9月27日（日本時間28日）までで全日程が終了した。ワールドシリーズ3連覇を目指すロサンゼルス・ドジャースは、最終戦のサンフランシスコ・ジャイアンツ戦で今季100勝目（62敗）を記録し、ポストシーズンはナ・リーグ第2シードとして、10月3日に初戦を戦う地区シリーズから出場する。 【画像】大谷翔平の妻、田中真美子が輝いた“現役バスケ選手時代”を厳選フォトで一挙紹介 ドジャースのポストシーズンを勝ち上がっていく上で、カギを握る存在がやはり、大谷翔平だ。今月に入り、右上腕の炎症により負傷者リスト（IL）登録で戦列を離れた。23日のサンディエゴ・パドレス戦での復帰後、5試合で本塁打こそ出ていないものの、4試合で安打を記録している。 打者専念で臨む今季のポストシーズン、大谷は本来の主砲としての働きを見せることができるのか。メジャー公式サイト『MLB.com』も最終戦終了後に掲載された特集記事において、大谷の現在のコンディションについて論じている。 同メディアは、シーズン最終盤のパフォーマンスを振り返り、「右上腕二頭筋と左膝の負傷が長引いたことで15日間の負傷者リスト（IL）入りし、そこから復帰した後の5試合では、打席で本来の姿をあまり見せられなかった」などと評価。また復帰後では、「21打数5安打、打率.238、8三振」の成績だったと記しており、さらに、「大谷はレギュラーシーズン全体では打率.275、OPS.889、30本塁打で終了した。本塁打はすべてIL入りする前に記録したものだった」と指摘する。 一方で、復帰後のより具体的な目的として、「最終的に重要視されたのは成績よりも、健康状態と打席での内容だった。マイナーでのリハビリ出場に近い意味合いを持っていた」と説明。加えて、バットスピードや平均打球速度は上昇傾向であるとして、ポジティブな要因も少なくないと同メディアは主張する。 また、最終戦終了後のデーブ・ロバーツ監督による、大谷の状態を語ったコメントも掲載。指揮官は地区シリーズ初戦を見据え、「これから数日が経てば、さらに状態が良くなることを期待している。だから土曜日を見据えれば、良い状態になっていると思う」などと話している。 そのうえで、改めて大谷のコンディションについて同メディアは「ポストシーズンの大舞台でプレーする姿を見る時までわからない」と綴っている。3度目の頂点を目指す戦いの中で、果たして大谷はどのようなスイングを見せてくれるのだろうか。 構成●THE DIGEST編集部

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dodgers' Josue De Paula update all but confirms his postseason roster spot
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers completed their sweep over the San Francisco Giants on Sunday in extra innings. It was their sixth time reaching the century-mark during the last decade, which is better than any American League team and second only to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League. The Dodgers now have four days to game plan before they take on either the Philadelphia Phillies or the Atlanta Braves in the NLDS at Dodger Stadium. There could be some surprises in store, especially on the bul
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers completed their sweep over the San Francisco Giants on Sunday in extra innings. It was their sixth time reaching the century-mark during the last decade, which is better than any American League team and second only to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League.
The Dodgers now have four days to game plan before they take on either the Philadelphia Phillies or the Atlanta Braves in the NLDS at Dodger Stadium.
There could be some surprises in store, especially on the bullpen front. Blake Treinen's season just ended with a shoulder issue, Edwin Díaz has enjoyed a resurgence since coming off the IL, Edgardo Henriquez is trending toward availability, and they still need to figure out the Roki Sasaki of it all.
But fans saw all of that coming. The more interesting roster development in the last week has been the battle of the No. 1 prospects: Josue De Paula vs. Dalton Rushing.
De Paula was optioned back to Triple-A after Shohei Ohtani came off the IL, and Rushing was officially reactivated from the IL ahead of the Giants series. De Paula, however, looks like he still has the upper hand here, and will be in LA during the bye week as the Dodgers consider all of their options.
Josue De Paula is on track to win Dodgers' postseason roster battle
The Dodgers are currently carrying three catchers: Rushing, Will Smith, and Hunter Feduccia. Whoever LA chooses to be the backup catcher, that player will be playing second fiddle to Smith (even more than they already do).
Last year, Ben Rortvedt started two games in the NL Wild Card Series while Smith came back from an injury, but he didn't make an appearance past Game 2 of the NLDS. Feduccia, though more dispensable than Rushing in most contexts, makes more sense in that role.
LA wants a big lefty bat they can keep on the bench, and De Paula established himself as the better bet almost immediately. At the same time, Rushing had the disadvantage of being on the IL, unable to state his own case.
The question is how the Dodgers will petition the Commissioner's Office to carry De Paula on the roster. He'll have to replace an injured player who's already served the minimum amount of time on the IL. In bringing Rushing back, the Dodgers needlessly complicated things.
But no doubt Andrew Friedman will figure it out. De Paula might only get a precious few at-bats throughout the month, but they clearly already trust him.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have a chance to repeat with Roberto Clemente Award winners this season.
Will Smith is the Dodgers’ nominee to win the prestigious honor this year, while Mookie Betts was named the 2025 Roberto Clemente Award winner.
The Roberto Clemente Award is considered baseball’s most prestigious individual honor. It is presented annually in recognition of the Major League player who best represents the game of baseball through extraordinary character, community involvement, philanthropy and positive contributions, both on and off the field.
Each team nominates one player to be considered for the league-wide award in tribute to Clemente’s achievements and character.
The Dodgers have had for players to win the award in history, with Betts being the most recent. Before that, it was Justin Turner who took the honor in 2022.
Major League Baseball continued its recognition of past Clemente Award winners and reached out to some of them on Instagram, asking what it means to be a winner.
Both Betts and Turner were among those who replied as part of the social media campaign.
“It means a lot… it means you are helping communities and it’s always cool to be recognized for the work you put in off the field,” Betts wrote in his reply to MLB. “Baseball is baseball, but being a good human is central to life.”
“For me it’s the greatest honor in the game because Roberto set the bar for what it means to take our platform, this beautiful gift of playing a game for a living, and use it to give back to those in need,” Turner wrote in his reply. “He took his star power and used it to lift up those in need and enduring difficult times! Roberto was a humanitarian who happened to be great at baseball!!!!”
Former Dodgers Curtis Granderson and Jimmy Rollins, who won the award with different teams, also shared their perspectives in the post. In addition, Nelson Cruz, who currently works in the Dodgers’ player development system, shared his insight.
Along with Betts and Turner, the other Dodgers to win the award were Clayton Kershaw (2012) and Steve Garvey (1981).
Roberto Clemente Award selection process
A panel of sportswriters and baseball dignitaries selects the winner of the Roberto Clemente Award. In addition, there is a fan vote element that counts as one vote among those cast by the blue-ribbon panel.
Fan voting ended on Sunday, the final day of the 2026 regular season.
The league-wide winner of the Roberto Clemente Award will be honored at the 2026 World Series following selection by the aforementioned panel.
It includes representatives from the commissioner’s office, Capital One, MLB-affiliated networks (MLB Network, FOX Sports, ESPN and TBS), MLB.com, National Baseball Hall of Fame, as well as Roberto’s children, Enrique, Luis and Roberto Clemente, Jr.
If you love our reporting, choose DodgerBlue.com as a preferred source on Google.

item.content:encoded:
| MLB 포스트시즌 대진표.(사진=MLB 공식 홈페이지) |
서부지구 1위 휴스턴은 3번 시드를 받았다. 와일드카드 순위에 따라 뉴욕 양키스와 보스턴 레드삭스, 시카고 화이트삭스가 각각 4~6번 시드에 자리했다. 와일드카드시리즈(WC·3전2승제)에서는 휴스턴과 화이트삭스, 양키스와 보스턴이 맞붙는다. 휴스턴-화이트삭스전 승자는 클리블랜드, 양키스-보스턴전 승자는 탬파베이와 DS에서 격돌한다.
내셔널리그(NL)에서는 밀워키 브루어스가 전체 승률 1위로 1번 시드를 거머쥐었고, 서부지구 우승팀 로스앤젤레스(LA) 다저스가 2번 시드로 DS 직행 티켓을 확보했다. 동부지구 챔피언 애틀랜타는 3번 시드에 자리했고, 샌디에이고와 시카고 컵스, 필라델피아 필리스가 차례로 4~6번 시드를 받았다.
한국 야구팬들의 시선은 포스트시즌 엔트리 발표로 향한다. 김하성과 송성문, 김혜성의 소속팀이 모두 가을야구 진출에 성공했지만 실제 포스트시즌 출전 여부는 로스트 승선에 달렸다. 이정후가 뛰는 샌프란시스코 자이언츠는 포스트시즌 진출에 실패하면서 시즌을 마쳤다.
가장 힘겨운 시즌을 보낸 선수는 김하성이다. 올해 초 빙판길에서 넘어지며 오른손 중지를 다친 그는 부상 여파 속에 정상적인 경기력을 되찾는 데 애를 먹었다. 김하성은 이날 마이애미 말린스와의 정규시즌 최종전에서 7번 타자 유격수로 선발 출전해 2타수 무안타에 그쳤지만 볼넷 2개를 골라내고 한 차례 홈을 밟았다. 올 시즌 최종 성적은 타율 0.116, 무홈런, 9타점이다.
다저스에서 빅리그 2년 차를 보낸 김혜성은 지난 5월 말 마이너리그로 내려간 뒤 시즌 막판까지 메이저리그 무대로 돌아오지 못했다. 빅리그에서는 타율 0.259, 1홈런, 11타점, 5도루를 기록했다. 다저스가 포스트시즌에 진출했지만 김혜성이 가을야구 엔트리에 이름을 올릴지가 관건이다.
올해 MLB 포스트시즌은 오는 30일부터 다음달 2일까지 열리는 WC로 막을 올린다. DS는 10 4~11일, 리그 챔피언십시리즈(LCS·7전4승제)는 10월 12~21일 진행된다. 양대 리그 챔피언이 맞붙는 월드시리즈(7전4승제)는 다음달 24일부터 시작된다.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] With Another 100 Win Season, Dave Roberts Joins Elite Company
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA — Dave Roberts has accomplished quite a bit during his tenure as Dodgers manager, but Sunday’s 5-1 victory over the Giants added another impressive achievement to his résumé. With the Dodgers reaching 100 victories, Roberts tied the all-time managerial record for most 100-win seasons, joining some of the most successful skippers in baseball history. item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO, CA — Dave Roberts has accomplished quite a bit during his tenure as Dodgers manager, but Sunday’s 5-1 victory over the Giants added another impressive achievement to his résumé.
With the Dodgers reaching 100 victories, Roberts tied the all-time managerial record for most 100-win seasons, joining some of the most successful skippers in baseball history.
Speaking with reporters following the regular-season finale, Roberts acknowledged the significance of the accomplishment while emphasizing the contributions of the players and organization that helped make it possible.
A Milestone Worth Celebrating
Asked whether reaching 100 wins carried significance even though the Dodgers had already secured their postseason position, Roberts made it clear that the milestone mattered.
“It does. It doesn’t change anything as far as our standing going forward in the postseason, but it’s still a nice feather in our cap to win 100 games.”
When informed that the victory tied him for the most 100-win seasons by any manager in major league history, Roberts reflected on the company he now keeps.
“Yeah, I guess I’m in some rare air, some good company. A lot of good players, a great organization, and it’s not easy, 100 games.
“There’s a lot of things that we had to go through this year, and we just continued to remain steadfast and play on. And so, yeah, that’s something to be proud of.”
Sunday’s victory provided a fitting conclusion to another successful regular season. Roberts particularly appreciated the pitching staff’s performance, with seven pitchers combining to hold San Francisco to one run while striking out 16.
“Obviously, we had a few guys that we wanted to stay away from. I thought the pitching did a remarkable job today. Bobby did a nice job picking up a couple innings, getting out of some stress there in the seventh, I think it was.
“And timely hitting. It didn’t look great early, but we hung in there as far as on the pitching side, and Alex with a big two-out hit, and then Andy finished up the season the right way.”
Preparing for Philadelphia or Atlanta
The Dodgers will now await the winner of the Phillies-Braves Wild Card Series, with Game 1 of the NLDS scheduled for Saturday at Dodger Stadium.
Roberts expects a competitive series between two familiar division rivals.
“When you start the season, those two teams were probably picked to be one-two in the East, and they’re very, very familiar with one another. So it’s going to be a good series.
“Obviously, the Phillies had to play to the end, but like I said, there’s a lot of familiarity, and all bets are off when you play within the division.
“So we’ll just sit back and take tomorrow off and have the workout on Tuesday. We’ll get to watch those guys, and then we’ll get to watch that other series during our workout.”
Getting the Big Bats Ready
Roberts also discussed the importance of the upcoming break for Freddie Freeman and Shohei Ohtani, both of whom have been working to find their offensive rhythm.
Regarding Ohtani, Roberts was encouraged by what he saw Sunday and believes the additional preparation will be valuable.
“I thought he looked fine. He looked better today. I do think that just getting some at-bats, however many he got since he came back, and then really just this week is going to be really crucial, I think, for Freddie. I think it’s going to be crucial for Sho.”
Roberts also emphasized that Ohtani emerged from his recent return to action healthy, which was the most important consideration.
“The process early was great. I thought in the middle of that he was kind of getting a little more anxious. I thought today the process was much better.
“But I think the main thing is that we feel that he came out of it healthy, and so you just expect the ensuing days he feels even better. When you look out to Saturday, I think he’ll be in a good spot.”
The Dodgers will make intrasquad games available during their preparation period, although Roberts said individual players will decide whether to participate.
For Roberts, the regular season concludes with another historic accomplishment and a chance to add to an already remarkable managerial legacy.
But the ultimate objective remains the same: 11 more wins and another World Series championship.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Miguel Rojas Reflects on (potentially) Final Regular Season Game
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA — Sunday’s 5-1 victory over the Giants was particularly meaningful for Miguel Rojas, who may have played the final regular-season game of his career. The veteran shortstop was visibly emotional during the broadcast, but after the Dodgers completed their sweep of San Francisco and reached 100 victories, his attention was already turning toward October. Speaking with reporters after the game, Rojas emphasized the importance of finishing the regular season strong and maintaining t
item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO, CA — Sunday’s 5-1 victory over the Giants was particularly meaningful for Miguel Rojas, who may have played the final regular-season game of his career. The veteran shortstop was visibly emotional during the broadcast, but after the Dodgers completed their sweep of San Francisco and reached 100 victories, his attention was already turning toward October.
Speaking with reporters after the game, Rojas emphasized the importance of finishing the regular season strong and maintaining the team’s momentum heading into the postseason.
“Yeah, it feels good. Finishing the season strong is something that we as a team put as a goal, not to take that foot off the gas pedal and play until the last out.
“I think it’s really important for us to continue to get momentum into the postseason, and winning is always contagious, and that’s what we’re looking for.
“We’re looking to win another 11 games for us to make history and do something really cool about our legacies and the city of LA.”
Five Days to Prepare Together
The Dodgers now have five days before Saturday’s NLDS opener, and Rojas believes the time together will provide opportunities that go beyond simply resting and recovering.
For the veteran infielder, some of the most valuable preparation comes from teammates sharing their knowledge and helping one another improve.
“Yeah, I mean, it’s going to be important because there’s so many things that we can actually take advantage of on workout days where you get feedback from your teammates more than anything.
“Not just the coaches or the game itself. You get together with your teammates and kind of swing in the cage with them and get together at the same time on the field and talk about pitches.
“You get to face your own pitchers and tell them about the movement of the pitches and ways that they can attack right-handed hitters, left-handed hitters, whatever it is.”
Rojas expressed confidence in the team’s preparation and its collective commitment to another championship run.
“I feel like we got a pretty good plan. We’re looking forward to spending three or four weeks together to finish the season, and we’re all going to make the sacrifice to be 100% in on this one.”
Bringing October Baseball Home to Los Angeles
With more than four million fans attending Dodgers games during the regular season, Rojas was also asked about the significance of securing home-field advantage for the NLDS.
For him, the opportunity to play more postseason games at Dodger Stadium is as much about rewarding the fans as it is about giving the team a competitive advantage.
“Yeah, they deserve it. It’s not just about us,” Rojas said, reflecting on the importance of giving fans the opportunity to experience the biggest postseason moments at home.
“It feels like we’re all really excited about being at home for more games and hopefully get to win at home.”
And while Sunday may have marked the conclusion of his regular-season career, Rojas was quick to point out that his Dodgers journey isn’t finished quite yet.
“We got some more games to play, so I’m really excited about that.”
For a player who has become such an important part of the Dodgers’ clubhouse, there’s still one more chapter to write. And as Freddie Freeman said after Sunday’s game, the team’s goal is to send Miggy out as a champion.
Eleven more wins.
